item.title: Friday the 13th Officially Sets Return With Legendary Director
item.description: After nearly 20 years at the bottom of Crystal Lake, an iconic slasher villain is finally returning to the big screen. Horror, Inc. announced that a new Friday the 13th movie is in production. The untitled film will be the 13th in the series, and it’s being directed by horror veteran Steve Miner, who previously helmed the second and third entries. We won’t have to wait long, because the movie is set for a global theatrical release in 2027.

item.title: UN refugee chief Barham Salih slams 'shameful' war in Sudan, urges 'political solution'
item.description: In an interview with FRANCE 24, UN refugee chief Barham Salih called the war in Sudan "shameful" and urged the world to end it. Salih also defended the "integrity of the asylum system".

item.title: Why I lied about having cancer – Blessing CEO
item.description: By Wasiu Rokibat Nigerian social media personality Blessing Okoro, popularly known as Blessing CEO, has sparked fresh reactions after admitting that she falsely claimed to have breast cancer which in turn led to financial assistance from members of the public. The relationship influencer made the revelation during an interview with social media activist Martins Vincent Otse, better known as VeryDarkMan. Speaking during the interview, Blessing explained that although medical examinations discovered a lump in her breast, the result showed that it was not cancerous. However, she admitted that she deliberately presented the condition as cancer to attract sympathy from fans. In her words, “I do not have cancer. I had gone for a check-up and they found a lump in my breast, but it was not cancerous. I took advantage of that and told the public that the lump was cancerous. I played an emotional game.” According to her, she initially suggested that she might sell some of her personal belongings, including her car and house, before members of the public encouraged her to share her bank details for financial assistance. Blessing also disclosed that donations began coming in from different individuals but stopped after VeryDarkMan publicly questioned her cancer claims and demanded evidence of her diagnosis. “People had empathy, I did not come out to beg for funds. I played an emotional game. I wanted funds but I didn’t come out directly to ask for funds. I started with pretending I wanted to sell my personal belongings, my house, my car; It was fans who reached out to me in my DM, asking me to put out my account number; that’s when I put out my account number.” “The donation was rolling in, until VeryDarkMan came and say you people cannot be donating money for Blessing when there is no evidence. Immediately, VeryDarkMan made that video, the donation stopped. I am not proud of what I did.” The confession has renewed public attention to the controversy, which began in March 2026 when the influencer announced that she had breast cancer and appealed for financial support. She had previously acknowledged receiving about N13 million in donations but maintained that there had been confusion surrounding her medical condition. The matter also attracted the attention of the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC), which arraigned her over alleged offences connected to the fundraising campaign. She pleaded not guilty to the charges. Vanguard News The post Why I lied about having cancer – Blessing CEO appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Nvidia scandal: How close was ex-CEO to Trump?
item.description: US lawmakers have called Jensen Huang to face their questions in December after the Nvidia ex-CEO quit over extramarital affairs, including one with a suspected Chinese spy. The Taiwanese-born businessman was a close informal adviser to President Donald Trump on AI and had spent years lobbying against curbs on sales of advanced AI chips to China for national security reasons. Just how close Huang was to Trump and the extent of the influence tech giants have on his administration are some of the questions that still need answering, says France 24’s Douglas Herbert.

item.title: Charlotte Hornets Draft Picks: List Of Future Picks In 2027
item.description: Jun 25, 2025; Brooklyn, NY, USA; Kon Knueppel stands with NBA commissioner Adam Silver after being selected as the fourth pick by the Charlotte Hornets in the first round of the 2025 NBA Draft at Barclays Center. Mandatory Credit: Brad Penner-Imagn Images | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Jimmy Vik The 2026-27 regular season has just begun for the Charlotte Hornets, but the front office has consistently preached a bright future for this franchise. The Hornets’ draft picks are the start of the massive flexibility Charlotte owns. The Hornets moving on from LaMelo Ball and Miles Bridges generated even more assets as the Hornets have taken a step back to further reevaluate their roster. It’s been tough to get a bird’s-eye view when the Hornets have sustained significant injuries in the past few months. With that said, here is the current outlook for the future Hornets’ draft picks in 2027. The Hornets’ First-Round Draft Pick Arsenal Is Ginormous in 2027 May 10, 2026; Chicago, IL, USA; A general view during the 2026 NBA Draft Lottery at Navy Pier. Mandatory Credit: David Banks-Imagn Images The Hornets have a massive opportunity in the 2027 NBA Draft , with the chance to walk away with three first-rounders — draft capital almost no one else in the league can touch that year. However, each of these picks comes with a few caveats. New Lottery System, But Hornets Draft Own First-Round Pick Charlotte owns their 2027 first-round pick. This is pretty straightforward. What will be different next year is the new NBA Draft Lottery system known as the 3-2-1 Lottery. Not only has the lottery teams been expanded to 16, but the ball allocation will be extremely different. Gone are the days when you could intentionally tank to be a bottom-three team in the league to guarantee a 14 percent chance to win the No. 1 overall pick. Now, the bottom three teams only have a 5.4 percent chance, while the next seven non-Play-In teams who hold a better record get an 8.1 percent chance. If the Draft Lottery commenced today, the Hornets would hold an 8.1 percent chance to snag the No. 1 pick. Nonetheless, there are no other stipulations to owning their own pick. After the draft, it’ll be interesting to see what players the Hornets would protect in an expansion draft . The Hornets have the second most firsts among teams. They create a $40.7M trade exception, the largest in league history. https://t.co/jidgIVc5vJ — Bobby Marks (@BobbyMarks42) June 25, 2026 Hornets’ 2 Incoming First-Round Picks Have Protections The Hornets also own two other protected first-round picks: one from the Dallas Mavericks and another from the Miami Heat. The pick from Dallas is top-2 protected, while Miami’s is lottery-protected. In layman’s terms, Charlotte will receive the Dallas pick as long as it lands anywhere outside of the No. 1 or 2 overall pick. item.title: South American U20 Championship: CONMEBOL draw puts Brazil in Group B
item.description: South American U20 Championship: CONMEBOL draw puts Brazil in Group B Brazil will be the top seed in Group B of the 2027 South American Championship. The groups were decided in a draw held this Friday (13) at CONMEBOL headquarters in Asunción, Paraguay. Colombia is the top seed in Group A. The tournament will take place from January 22 to February 7 in Medellín. The top four teams in the competition’s final stage will qualify for the World Cup in this age group, which will take place in September in Azerbaijan and Uzbekistan. Group B will feature Brazil, Argentina, Uruguay, Bolivia and Venezuela. Group A consists of Paraguay, Chile, Ecuador and Peru, alongside hosts Colombia. During the Brazilian Under-20 national team’s preparations in 2026, which included five squad call-ups, Brazil faced Bolivia twice at Granja Comary, winning both matches 2–0. Competition format The 2027 South American Under-20 Championship will be played in two stages: the group stage and the final stage. In the group stage, the ten participating teams are divided into Groups A and B, with five teams each. Matches will follow a single round-robin format, with every team playing each of the other teams in its group once. The top four teams in each group will advance to the final stage. In the final stage, the winner of each group will face the runner-up from the opposite group. The winners of these matches will automatically qualify for the World Cup and contest the tournament final. The losing semifinalists will face the winners of the crossover matches between the third- and fourth-placed teams in Groups A and B to determine the other two World Cup qualifiers. item.title: BON Roundtable: Can Texas carry its success over to Baton Rouge?
item.description: COLUMBIA, MISSOURI - NOVEMBER 07: Arch Manning #16 of the Texas Longhorns scrambles from Jason Dowell #92 of the Missouri Tigers during the first half at Faurot Field at Memorial Stadium on November 07, 2026 in Columbia, Missouri. (Photo by Jay Biggerstaff/Getty Images) | Getty Images Last week, this roundtable was down on the Longhorns’ chances of doing what it takes to salvage a frustrating season. Does Saturday’s performance against Missouri change your outlook for the final three regular-season games? Daniel Seahorn (@DanielSeahorn) — Sark finally showing some offensive adjustments certainly gives a glimmer of hope. On top of that, Arch Manning is coming off his best game of the year and looked sharp. LSU on the road at night will be a tough test, but I feel like the team’s trajectory is pointing up after the win in Columbia. Jacob Neidg (@jneidig_2) — Yes, it does. The offense showed real life against a solid defense without four starters. Only Coleman is expected back, but the results were still encouraging. More importantly, it also put Texas in a position to drop one more game and still be included in the playoffs. This LSU team might be the most talented squad Texas has played since the Ohio State game, and Texas can afford to lose, possibly. Wescott Eberts (@SBN_Wescott) – Yeah, it does. I was concerned about the injuries in the secondary against a good Missouri passing game, but Warren Roberson held up well despite the Tigers trying to go after him, and he combined with Graceson Littleton, who was in danger of missing the game, on the huge fumble return that put the game away. On offense, seeing Steve Sarkisian fully pivot back to some schemes that have worked well for the Longhorns in the past, along with efficient play from Arch Manning, has me feeling better about Texas winning the last three games. Gerald Goodridge (@ghgoodridge) — It looks like Sark has decided to supplement the run game with short passing and screens, which I think is where this offense can thrive. That allowed Texas to play complementary football for the first time all year, so it was exciting. We know the defense will be solid at worst each week, so if the offense is competent enough to score four times, I feel Texas can succeed and close out the year. Arch Manning played the best game of the year, and the Texas offense looked, dare I say, competent against the Tigers. What stood out most to you about how the Longhorns approached the game plan Saturday? Daniel — The passing game was quick and didn’t require Arch to hold onto the ball for an eternity with long developing routes downfield. He got the ball out quickly to his playmakers and gave them a chance in space. On top of that, Raleek Brown was able to make the offensive line right as a ball carrier. He took advantage of his expanded role within the offense with Hollywood Smothers on the shelf for the remainder of the year. item.title: Saturday's Claiming Crown gives workaday horses a place in the sun
item.description: Juryoku Pierrot, shown winning the Japanese Oaks in May, returns in Sunday's Grade 1 Queen Elizabeth II Cup at Kyoto Racecourse. Photo by and courtesy of Katsumi Saito Nov. 13 (UPI) -- Saturday's Claiming Crown races at Churchill Downs give the sport's workaday horses a chance at glory and slightly inflated paychecks. Unlike the Breeders' Cup, where entry primarily is through success in graded stakes races, the Claiming Crown heats are open only to horses who have started in claiming races for specific amounts in the recent past. Nine races, two of them on dirt, offer purses ranging up to $200,000 for the Claiming Crown Jewel on dirt and $175,000 for the Claiming Crown Emerald on turf. The races draw from around the country and are designed to be competitive. This year, the nine races drew 113 entries whose combined running lines show performances at 55 racetracks. The Claiming Crown is a cooperative effort of the National Horsemen's Benevolent and Protective Association and the Thoroughbred Owners and Breeders' Association. This will be the 28th running. Victory Achieved, shown winning the Nearctic Stakes in her last start, is back for Saturday's Grade II Kennedy Road Stakes at Woodbine. Photo by Michael Burns, courtesy of Woodbine Otherwise, there's action for 2-year-olds from coast to coast, and some scattered stakes events are mixed in. On the international front, turn to Japan, Bahrain and Australia. The 2-year-olds Saturday's Belmont Park program features $175,000 turf sprints for 2-year-olds and 2-year-old fillies. Del Mar on Saturday has the $100,000 Desi Arnaz for 2-year-old fillies at 7 furlongs on the dirt. Sunday's $100,000 Grade III Bob Hope is open to all juveniles at the same distance. Saturday's Gulfstream Juvenile Sprint also is on the dirt, at 6 furlongs. Woodbine Saturday's $200,000 (Canadian) Grade II bet365 Kennedy Road goes at 6 furlongs on the all-weather track. Mark Casse trains the favorites, Grade II Nearctic winner Victory Achieved and My Boy Prince, closely followed by Wesley Ward's upwardly mobile Arbiter. Laurel Park Saturday's $100,000 Thirty Eight Go Go Stakes features fillies and mares at 1 1/16 miles on the dirt. Around the world, around the clock Japan Sunday's Grade 1 Queen Elizabeth II Cup at Kyoto Racecourse offers a rare meeting of three Japanese Oaks winners. Among those set to face off in the 2,200-meter race for fillies and mares are this year's winner of the Oaks, formally the Yushun Himba, Juryoku Pierrot (JPN), the 2025 winner, Kamunyak (JPN) and the 2024 winner Cervina (JPN). While none is a runaway favorite, Juryoku Pierrot has won all three starts since being switched from dirt to grass and used an impressive late run to land the Oaks. Hoever, she has not run since that race May 24. Bahrain The kingdom celebrates its first Group 1 race with Friday's newly elevated Bahrain International Trophy and a field topped by Victorious Forever's Wimbledon Hawkeye. item.title: Alabama Basketball vs Seton Hall: 3 Keys, How to Watch
item.description: NEWARK, NEW JERSEY - NOVEMBER 2: Roddie Anderson #23 of the Seton Hall Pirates dribbles the ball against Jordan Mathews #11 of the Saint Peter's Peacocks during the second half of a college basketball game at Prudential Center on November 2, 2026 in Newark, New Jersey. (Photo by Porter Binks/Getty Images) | Getty Images Nate Oats and the Crimson Tide welcome their first power-conference opponent of the season to Coleman Coliseum Friday night, as the Seton Hall Pirates come to Tuscaloosa for a matchup between undefeated teams. The two programs have split two prior meetings, with Seton Hall taking the last one back in 2010. Head coach Shaheen Holloway begins his fifth season, having returned to his alma mater in 2022 after a successful stint at Saint Peter’s, where in 2022 he guided the Peacocks to the Elite Eight as a No. 15 seed. His time at Seton Hall has been a bit of a roller coaster. After winning 25 games with a NIT championship in 2024, the Pirates stumbled to a miserable 7-25 record the following season. Holloway responded with an impressive turnaround in 2025-26, guiding Seton Hall to a 21-12 record while taking home a Big East Coach of the Year award. Unfortunately they were one of the first four out in March and decided to take their ball and go home rather than go for another NIT. This one will be a study in contrasting styles, really for the first time this season. Unlike Oats, Holloway isn’t particularly interested in turning basketball games into track meets. According to WalterNolan , Seton Hall ranks 325th in pace of play while Alabama is the 11th fastest team in America. The Pirates get after it on defense, allowing just 54.7 points per game, but their offense has been less than stellar. If Alabama is able to get out in transition, this one could be another walk, but Seton Hall will undoubtedly do everything within their power to drag the Tide into a street fight. Like everyone else, Seton Hall is breaking in a bunch of new faces. Holloway lost his top four scorers, representing 41 points per game to replace. Among the losses was do-everything point guard Budd Clark, who is now at Ole Miss and scored 15 against Alabama in exhibition play. This is one of the more extreme rebuilds you’ll find as reserve Trey Parker is the only scholarship player who returns from last season. The Pirates are easily the toughest opponent that Alabama has faced to date, ranking 79th on KenPom. Alabama’s three previous foes are all outside the top 150 currently. Players to Watch: PG Roddie Anderson, 6’3″ senior Anderson is on his fourth stop after UC San Diego, Boise State, and Xavier. He leads the Pirates in scoring at 17 per game, more than double anyone else on the roster, and has been quite consistent. He’s also been on fire from deep, with 10 made threes in only 18 attempts. item.title: Former Michigan QB Colin Hurley plans to enter transfer portal
item.description: Former Michigan quarterback Colin Hurley plans to enter the transfer portal, his agent Brian Davis tells On3. Hurley previously medically retired due to a concussion but is ready to make his return to football. Hurley is a former four-star recruit and LSU transfer. Hurley has been enrolled at Michigan this fall, taking classes after medically retiring in the spring. Hurley transferred in from LSU this past offseason and went through winter conditioning and spring practices. The 6-foot-1, 218-pound Miami native spent two seasons with LSU, after reclassifying and joining the Tigers’ program at 16 years old in January 2024. “Colin has worked hard on his health and is excited to come back to the sport he loves,” Davis told On3. “Colin has two years of eligibility left and can’t wait to play again.” During the recruiting process, Hurley had interest from Alabama, Florida, Georgia, Miami, Ohio State and others. The former Jacksonville (Fla.) Trinity Christian Academy star was a two-time state champion in high shcool and threw for over 5,000 yards in his career. Hurley was also an Elite 11 finalist and a U.S. Army All-American. The college football transfer portal officially opens on Jan. 4 for a 10-day window.

item.title: MLB rumors: Mets bring pokerface to Tarik Skubal table, but nobody is buying it
item.description: MLB rumors: Mets bring pokerface to Tarik Skubal table, but nobody is buying it appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The New York Mets are reportedly stepping up their pursuit of Tarik Skubal , but they’re playing down their chances of signing him. Rival teams aren’t convinced, however, with New York viewed as a serious threat to the Los Angeles Dodgers in the race for the ace. According to Bob Nightengale of USA Today, the Mets are downplaying their chances of landing Skubal. However, rival executives reportedly believe New York could present the Dodgers’ toughest competition. The Dodgers, San Diego Padres, and Toronto Blue Jays also have meetings scheduled with Skubal before Thanksgiving. That growing interest could turn his free agency into an expensive bidding war. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Skubal and agent Scott Boras have reportedly made their contract expectations clear. They aren’t interested in a short-term agreement, with teams needing to offer more than $325 million to seriously enter negotiations. That figure would surpass the $325 million deal Yoshinobu Yamamoto signed with Los Angeles in December 2023, setting a new benchmark for pitchers. For New York, the financial demands present another major offseason decision. Owner Steve Cohen has demonstrated his willingness to spend, particularly after the Mets missed the postseason in 2026. Still, signing Skubal wouldn’t automatically address every weakness. The Mets need additional pitching depth beyond one superstar , making their offseason strategy especially important. For now, the Mets may continue minimizing expectations publicly. But with a meeting approaching and rival teams watching closely, their reported interest remains difficult to dismiss. Whether New York ultimately submits a record-setting offer could determine how seriously its poker face holds up. item.title: Patriots takeaways from Germany: What Mike Vrabel said about A.J. Brown playing in Munich
item.description: MUNICH – After making the trip to Munich, will A.J. Brown play on Sunday against the Detroit Lions? That was the big question facing the Patriots on Friday. Temperatures dipped into the low 40s as the team held a full 90-minute practice at the FC Bayern Munich training facility. After flying into Munich on Thursday, and holding a 60-minute walkthrough, Mike Vrabel’s team picked up the pace. The Patriots coach said he felt “pretty good” about the status of A.J. Brown and Rhamondre Stevenson after watching the two players at Thursday’s practice. “So, let’s go through today and see where that goes and then meet with (trainer) Jim (Whalen) and meet with players,” Vrabel said. Brown has played in three of nine games this season. The Pro Bowl receiver missed four weeks in a row after suffering a high ankle sprain in the team’s regular-season opener in Seattle. After returning, and playing twice in five days, Brown’s been dealing with a nagging knee injury. The receiver missed two weeks of practices and the Patriots matchups against Miami and Green Bay. Brown returned to practice on Wednesday before flying with the team on Thursday. “I think the more that we can get everybody back, I think the more that it contributes to what we feel like we want to be as a team,” Vrabel said when asked about having Brown at practice. “And one guy certainly doesn’t make the difference, but it’s certainly the more that we can get guys back. It’s exciting that the pieces can start to build and come together. So, you know, we’ll see where things go today. And hopefully, you know, those guys that haven’t been with us or maybe got hurt last week, that could be available.” In three games, Brown’s caught nine passes for 101 yards. He’d be a huge boost for Drake Maye and the offense, if healthy. After dealing with two different injuries, Vrabel was asked if the team needed to protect Brown from himself when it comes to how much they play him when he does return. RELATED: Early data projections: Pats head to Germany seeking a huge rebound in Week 10 vs. Lions “I mean, again, we just have to try to see where things go and how they feel, and we got to trust them a little bit, how they tell us and also have a plan for each and every guy,” Vrabel said. “I think it’s kind of see how it goes.” Here are the top takeaways from the Patriots’ second day in Munich: Will Rhamondre Stevenson play? If Brown plays, it’d be a huge boost for the offense. The same can be said if Rhamondre Stevenson is cleared to play on Sunday. The running back suffered a knee injury last weekend against Green Bay. On Monday, ESPN and the NFL Network reported Stevenson would miss weeks due to his injury. However, Stevenson flew with the team to Munich and practiced the last two days. Stevenson’s presence here has been surprising. Vrabel said the veteran is working hard to play and admires his attitude. “I think we’re just always looking for guys that are looking for ways in as opposed to ways out,” Vrabel said. “

item.title: Mauricio Pochettino Leaves USMNT to Join Manchester United 1 Day After Club Fires Manager
item.description: Mega Mauricio Pochettino is saying goodbye to the United States men’s national team after just two years. U.S. Soccer announced during a press conference on Friday, November 13, that Pochettino, 54, would be stepping down to join Manchester United as its new manager. Pochettino called it “one of the most difficult decisions” to make, but added, “A decision that in some part is a sad decision, and in another part is we are professional and we are trying to find the next step and trying to make your dreams come true.” The news comes just one day after the Premier League team fired its former manager , Michael Carrick . Carrick was let go on November 12, just 15 games into his two-year contract, which he signed back in May. According to ESPN , a representative for Pochettino informed Manchester United of a $10 million release clause in his contract with U.S. Soccer, which United CEO Omar Berrada agreed to. Pochettino, who is from Argentina, was reportedly the only candidate to fill the vacant role and was the “unanimous choice” by the club’s leadership. Mega “The Argentinian is renowned for his high-intensity, attacking style of football, his dedication to building strong, cohesive teams and his outstanding record of developing individual players,” a statement from United read. “Pochettino has consistently performed at the highest level of football across multiple leagues.” Pochettino signed a 2.5 year deal with Man U and is set to take on his new role beginning when the team faces Liverpool in Anfield on November 22. item.title: Rhamondre Stevenson injury update: Patriots RB practices in Munich days after knee injury
item.description: MUNICH – As the Patriots warmed up before their first practice at the FC Bayern Munich training facility, Rhamondre Stevenson was out on the field in his jersey, running off to the side. The Patriots crossed the Atlantic Ocean without three teammates – Carlton Davis (knee), Ben Brown (knee) and TreVeyon Henderson (illness). All three were ruled out for Sunday’s matchup. Several players limited with injuries made the trip to Munich. That wasn’t a surprise. Seeing Stevenson present for the walkthrough, however, was. On Monday, ESPN and the NFL Network reported that Stevenson suffered a plantaris tendon issue in the back of his knee and was expected to miss a few weeks. But come Thursday morning , the running back was listed as a limited practice participant. “I think that speaks to first off, the media right now, really knowing 100 percent what they’re talking about a lot of the time,” Maye said. “And then first off, just of a guy that wants to be out there, wants to be back for a team, and that’s what we’re in the midst of, trying to make a run here and win a big one before the bye. So this is a time for players, a lot of players on this team that are trying to get out there, play with teammates and knowing they need a great player to help us out.” Stevenson ran for 32 yards and had three catches for 46 yards with a touchdown before suffering the knee injury against the Green Bay Packers. The next day, Mike Vrabel said the Patriots were awaiting the results of Stevenson’s MRI. RELATED: Early data projections: Pats head to Germany seeking a huge rebound in Week 10 vs. Lions The running back didn’t practice on Wednesday, but made the trip to Munich. And after the overnight flight, he was at practice with his teammates. “He’s a dog, man,” receiver DeMario Douglas said. “I know some people that probably like, I ain’t even going to try (to play), you but his situation, man, I be talking to him (and he’s) like, I’m going to try. I’m going to do what I can. He’s working, he’s getting better. So, you know, when the time comes, I know he, he working to get better than.” Stevenson leads the Patriots in rushing yards (399) and is fourth on the team in receiving with 258 yards. His four total touchdowns are tied for the most on the team. If he can’t play, the Patriots would lean on Corey Kiner, Lan Larison and Terrell Jennings at running back. “Anytime you lose players like that, you feel it because he’s such a valuable part of everything you do,” Patriots offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels said. “But that’s why we have a lot of guys that are taking reps in practice. We’ve had a lot of guys doing that all year long. They know what to do. It might not be the same volume of experience that certainly Rhamondre has, but we got a lot of guys in that room that we have confidence in.” McDaniels was asked about the possibility of playing without Stevenson. item.title: ‘Unbelievable’: Chris Finch shares what Ayo Dosunmu has done that most others just cannot do
item.description: Photo by Carmen Mandato/Getty Images Ayo Dosunmu has become a key player for the Minnesota Timberwolves this season. Anthony Edwards’ absence was viewed by many as a massive blow, and the Wolves did show some signs of weakness without their main man in attack. However, Dosunmu has taken much of that burden lately, and his performances for Chris Finch’s side have been really impressive. Now, the T-Wolves head coach has shared what separates him from many others. Chris Finch says Ayo Dosunmu’s ‘readiness factor is elite’ The Minnesota Timberwolves acquired Dosunmu from the Chicago Bulls in February this year. The former Illinois Fighting Illini star was initially brought in as a rotation option, but injuries to key players have often given him starting opportunities. Dosunmu has always been able to do a decent job for the Wolves, but his performances have gone up a level this season. Why? Finch believes it’s all down to his readiness factor – most players need some time to get going, but Dosunmu is different. He can hit the ground running at any point. Finch said in a press conference: “He has met every need that we’ve had along the way, whether it’d be a guy to come in and give us depth or step up in the playoffs when people went down, and now, without Anthony starting, just being the guy you can put the ball in his hands on demand and he gets you something. “He continues to have an end-to-end game and is a good fit alongside Melo in that regard. He fits so well with so many different lineups. You don’t even have to think about putting him out there to play on or off the ball. He’s just kind of met every moment we’ve needed him to meet. “He’s an unbelievable professional, and his readiness factor is elite. “A lot of players might spin their wheels a little bit before they’re able to produce what you need them to produce. He’s always been, right away, whatever we needed.” In his last eight games for the Timberwolves, Dosunmu has averaged 21.1 points, five rebounds and 3.2 assists. He has formed a great partnership with LaMelo Ball and is proving to be really effective. The Wolves have now won five games in a row. That is an impressive run on its own, but to do it without Edwards makes it so much better. Dosunmu deserves all the praise in the world, and if he can keep it going along with Ball, the T-Wolves will be in a great position by the time Edwards is back. item.title: Emotional Mauricio Pochettino in tears over USA exit after accepting Manchester United manager role
item.description: Mauricio Pochettino Press Conference - Getty Images Sport Mauricio Pochettino could not hide his emotions during a heartfelt farewell to the United States national team, breaking down in tears just moments after being confirmed as the new Manchester United manager. The Argentine has agreed to a two-and-a-half-year deal at Old Trafford, marking a stunning return to the Premier League as the successor to Michael Carrick. A bittersweet departure for Pochettino The appointment of Pochettino at Manchester United has brought an end to his successful stint with the United States national team, but the transition has clearly taken a personal toll. During his first media appearance since the news broke, the 54-year-old was visibly moved as he addressed his impending departure. Speaking to reporters on Friday, the emotional weight of the announcement was evident - a raw reaction reflecting his deep connection to the American setup he has led since September 2024. While most managerial tears follow a dismissal, Pochettino noted that walking away from his international post weighed heavily on him, even as the lure of Old Trafford proved impossible to ignore following Thursday's sacking of Carrick, who departed after an eight-match winless run in the Premier League . Raw emotion on display in final presser Pochettino will officially take the reins at Old Trafford on November 19 once the USA's upcoming fixtures conclude, setting up a blockbuster debut away at Liverpool on Sunday, November 22. Reflecting on his impending departure, he admitted: 'Normally it's the opposite. You're sacked and you cry because you want to stay. For this case it's the opposite. It's a really tough decision, but at the same time I'm excited for that step.' Pochettino took the opportunity to express his gratitude to those he worked with during a transformative period for American soccer. He spoke directly to the people who had supported his vision, emphasising the bond formed over the last two years. 'The staff and the players, I want to say thank you so much for the last two years. You made me feel really happy sharing an amazing project. It's difficult now for me to finish,' he added during the emotional briefing. Building a legacy with the Stars and Stripes Before officially taking the reins at Old Trafford, the 54-year-old will oversee the USA's fixtures against Haiti, bringing the curtain down on a spell that began in September 2024. Initially contracted through this summer's World Cup, he earned a four-year extension until the end of the 2030 finals after guiding the Stars and Stripes to the last 16, boasting an impressive record of 22 wins from 35 matches ahead of this week's double-header. Addressing the difficulty of the transition, Pochettino highlighted the shared growth within the federation. item.title: Egor Chinakhov needs to trust the process
item.description: PITTSBURGH, PA - OCTOBER 03: Egor Chinakhov #59 of the Pittsburgh Penguins skates during the game against the Montréal Canadiens at PPG PAINTS Arena on October 3, 2026 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Joe Sargent/NHLI via Getty Images) | NHLI via Getty Images Goalie Sergei Murashov stole the show for the Pittsburgh Penguins in their 3-2 shootout win against the San Jose Sharks on Wednesday night. He was their best overall player, and one of the biggest reasons they won the game. It was an encouraging development for the young goalie as he seems to be finding his confidence . While he was keeping pucks out of the net and giving the Penguins a chance, their best non-goalie was forward Egor Chinakhov, even if it did not show itself on the stat sheet. He was everywhere the entire game, creating chances, forcing turnovers, winning puck races, and just making an impact every time he was on the ice. It has been a trend for him lately, and he is one of the players on the Penguins that is arguably playing significantly better than his season-long stat line would have you believe. The stat line itself (three goals, two assists in 15 games) is a little underwhelming given the way he finished the 2025-26 season and the expectations it created for this season. I do not believe that will continue. He is playing like a guy that is on the verge of breaking out and going on a goal-scoring binge very, very soon. Aside from the burst he is showing and the speed that is on display, a lot of the underlying numbers are painting the picture of a guy that’s just been a little unlucky so far. At least as it relates to his own individual goal-scoring. The shots and shot attempts are still there. The rush-chances are still there. Among Penguins players that have played at least 100 minutes of 5-on-5 ice-time, the only players averaging more shots on goal per 60 minutes are Nicholas Robertson and Rickard Rakell. Nobody is averaging more total shot attempts than his 19.1 (and nobody is really even close; Rakell is the only player over 16 attempts per 60 minutes). Nobody is generating more chances off the rush than his 1.27 per 60 minutes (and again, nobody is even close; Rakell is second at 0.46 and Ben Kindel is third at 0.32). Across the entire league, his 5-on-5 shot attempts/60 are 13th in the league. His rush attempts are first in the league. That is what you want to see from him. You want to see his speed generating chances. It is. You want to see a guy with his shot unleashing it. He is. The thing that is crushing him right now is the simple reality that nothing is finding the back of the net. At least not yet. There is an element of luck to it that is not going in his favor right now. He had one goal disallowed on a borderline goalie interference call earlier in the season. He has hit at least three or four posts this season, including one that echoed throughout the entire San Jose region on Wednesday. He has also only scored on 4.35 percent of his shots shots

item.title: Mauricio Pochettino reveals when Man United contacted him about replacing Michael Carrick
item.description: Mauricio Pochettino struggled to fight off tears as he held his first press conference since being confirmed as Michael Carrick ’s managerial successor at Manchester United . Pochettino will leave his post as United States manager at the end of the current international break, joining up with United on 18 November after the club moved to replace Carrick, who was sacked on Thursday. Pochettino penned a four-year extension in the summer that was meant to keep him with the USA until the 2030 World Cup, but United triggered his release clause after a hashing out an agreement with the Argentinian, and will pay US Soccer compensation worth an initial $7m (£5.3m). Asked what made him swap the USA for United despite committing his future earlier this year, Pochettino said: "It's obvious. I never said I wanted to go back but they know there aren't too many opportunities that happen in your career like Manchester United. When it arrives, it's difficult to turn down. Mauricio Pochettino was in tears as he spoke for the first time since making the switch to Man United (Getty) "When we decided together to extend our commitment, it was a commitment for the federation, just in case. We were very committed. It was to help the federation, just in case that didn't work for four years." Pochettino said contact from United was first made on Sunday afternoon, the same day as the Villa draw, insisting that he was “very transparent” with US Soccer throughout the process. "All was so quick. Sunday afternoon, there started to be some contact. We were very transparent [with US Soccer],” he said. "We’ll have time next week to talk about the job at Manchester United. It’s much better to talk now about US Soccer." The former Tottenham and Chelsea manager nevertheless opted against speaking at length about his United move, which he described as “the most difficult decisions of my career”, instead focussing on Haiti and his time in the USA setup. "We have time this week to talk about the job in Manchester United but I think it's much better to talk about us, about US Soccer,” he said. “We have two games ahead and now it's focus on this." He will remain in charge for the United States’ two Concacaf Nations League fixtures against Haiti during the international break, with an away match on 14 November and a home match in Cincinnati on 18 November. Pochettino will then report to Carrington shortly after, with his official start date being on 18 November, ahead their next Premier League match against Liverpool at Anfield on 22 November. He also explained why he decided to see out the rest of the international break in the USA dugout, saying it was out of respect for his players and staff. Pochettino will see out the rest of the international break in the USA dugout (Getty) “Because before [we are] professional, we are a person,” he added. “The emotional link between us is to show the commitment and respect and the love, even if we take a decision that is not the best for one part.

item.title: Tearful Pochettino on 'difficult' decision to leave USA for Man Utd
item.description: Mauricio Pochettino was emotional during his USA news conference [Getty Images] Mauricio Pochettino says the decision to leave his role as boss of the USA national team to become Manchester United head coach was "one of the most difficult" of his career. The Argentine was announced as Michael Carrick's successor at Old Trafford on Friday, with sources telling BBC Sport he has signed a two-and-a-half-year contract. United paid a release clause in the region of £7.4m to extract Pochettino from his USA contract, with a further payment being made for his backroom staff. Pochettino only signed a new four-year deal with the USA in the summer, but will depart for Manchester after leading the national team in matches against Haiti on 14 and 18 November. The 54-year-old broke down in tears during his first news conference after his move to United was confirmed, and thanked the US Soccer Federation for its support. "It's difficult to talk now," he said. "I'm a very emotional guy. It's a very sad decision. "But we are professionals and we are trying to make our dreams come true." Asked why he signed a new deal with the national side only to accept United's offer, Pochettino said the chance to manage at Old Trafford was too good to reject. "I never said I wanted to go back but they know there aren't too many opportunities that happen in your career like Manchester United," he said. "When it arrives, it's difficult to turn down." Carrick was sacked on Thursday after United's worst start to a domestic campaign in 40 years, which has left them languishing in 18th place in the Premier League. Pochettino will inherit a side that have won just once in 10 league matches this season and sit just one point above bottom-placed Sunderland. His first match in charge will be an away match against Liverpool on 22 November. How Ferguson-inspired Pochettino can succeed where Carrick failed at Man Utd A decade in the making Pochettino's arrival at Old Trafford marks the end of a decade-long courtship. Thriving during an 18-month stint at Southampton, he led the Saints to eighth place during his only full season on the south coast. Tottenham moved quickly to appoint one of the most promising young coaches in Europe in 2014, and it was in north London that his reputation rocketed. The club had finished in the top four just twice in the 22 years before his appointment, but Pochettino led them there four times in his five full seasons. It was two years into his time in the capital that United first considered a move for Pochettino. The Argentine dined with legendary former United boss Sir Alex Ferguson in Mayfair, London just weeks before Louis van Gaal was sacked as Red Devils boss. The club ultimately decided to appoint Jose Mourinho, and Pochettino was again overlooked when the Portuguese departed in 2018, with Ole Gunnar Solskjaer impressing so much in an interim role that he was given the job more permanently. item.title: Dan Campbell pitches football, Lions to German fans
item.description: MUNICH, Germany — Between his time as a player, assistant and now a head coach, Dan Campbell is approaching three decades spent in the NFL. All that time in and around football makes Campbell uniquely qualified to pitch the game he loves to Germans, many of whom are being introduced to the sport for the first time this week, as the Detroit Lions and New England Patriots will play at Allianz Arena on Sunday, Nov. 15. "This game gave me a life," Campbell said Friday, Nov. 13, addressing reporters in Munich. "I was not a superstar, I was not a speed demon. I've got size, I played tight end, so you do a little bit of everything. But it gave me an opportunity to make a life and do something I absolutely loved with a group of guys, in any given time, 53 men in that locker room that you all have the same goal and you're all going in the same directions, and the blood and the sweat and the tears that it requires on a daily basis to be great are the things you never forget." Added Campbell, who tapped his fist on the table in front him as he became more fired up: "It builds character. It builds character in your team, it builds character as an individual, and it allows you to overcome anything in life that may come your way. Unfortunately, and I tell the team all the time, one day you're gonna get hit, you're gonna get rocked with something really tough in your life. I hate to say it, I don't want it to happen, none of us do, but you will, and you're going to have to be the rock. "But you're going to know how to overcome it, and you know who you can lean on, too, your brothers who have gone through everything you had to go through here. I just think it's special that way, and it gives guys an opportunity that may not have all the bells and whistles, all that, just because they do all the little things right and they maximize everything that they have and their ability. That's the best way I could do it or say it." More: Lions' Dan Campbell delivers lesson in how not to use German profanity The matchup with the Patriots on Sunday is Detroit's first game overseas since it played the Kansas City Chiefs at London's Wembley Stadium in 2015. It's the sixth NFL game to be played in Germany, and the third in Munich. The Lions took an overnight flight to Germany, departing Thursday evening and arriving Friday morning. Campbell also described the city of Detroit, and what, to him, makes it a special place. "It's a blue-collar city, and we have blue-collar fans," Campbell said. "They're very much all about hard work. We don't have the beach, we don't have all this — now, the summers are unbelievable. But things come a little bit harder out in that area. ... It's people that'll do anything for you, they'd give you the shirt off their back if you needed it. They're all about doing the hard stuff." item.title: Everything Texans DC Matt Burke said ahead of Week 10's game vs. Browns
item.description: Here's everything Houston Texans defensive coordinator Matt Burke said ahead of Week 10's matchup against the Cleveland Browns , including the play of tight end Harold Fannin Jr. and quarterback Deshaun Watson . Q: On whether the defense is capable of preforming like they did last season Matt Burke: "Yeah, I think so. I would hope so. That's again, that's our goal obviously and I think there was a step in the right direction last week from some of the things that we were trying to get accomplished. Every season is different and I don't think you can always chase what you had or whatnot, but we're always trying to chase perfection and I think there's a lot of games left to keep growing and I think if we stay on the trend that we started on last week, I think we hopefully are heading in that direction.” Q: On Cleveland Browns QB Deshaun Watson Burke: "He’s making a lot of plays really. I haven't gone against him in a while as a coach. I'm just really diving into that a little bit. Especially obviously with some of the injuries he's had, like really moving around really well, I would say like the making plays with his legs and off-scheduling the run game, obviously transferring the offense kind of from Baltimore, Coach [Todd] Monken and that sort of thing. There's a lot of like carry over and so how they're trying to use them. He has the danger of making a lot of guys miss in the pocket, we've seen a lot of plays where he's dipping the shoulder and guys are flying by him. He's shrugging guys off and then getting out. That part of it was kind of, I don't want to say surprising, but hadn't really remember seeing a lot of that. He’s really doing a really good job with using his legs, both in the run game, pass game, getting away from the rush, all those sort of things. He hasn't thrown a lot of interceptions, taking care of the ball pretty well. Always has had the arm and can make all those throws, so that's still there. I just thought the other stuff has really stood out to me on tape.” Q: On what leads to DT Tommy Togiai recording a high number of tackles Burke: “I think it was probably the same last year. Did he lead the league in tackles last year or something close? I think it's probably since Tommy's been here, he's been one of our most consistent performers across the whole team, I would say and he does it in practice. He does in games. For a defensive tackle, he's got really good awareness. He's just got like really good football savvy. I'd say him and ‘Rank’ [DT Sheldon Rankins] are two of the better ones I've been around from a defensive tackle position that just have an understanding of sort of big picture how the run schemes are set up. It's not just kind of blindly just trying to be in there and either occupy space or wreck shop. They're both really good with their hands. Tommy just has a really good, good eyes for the ball. item.title: Oregon has 3 quarterbacks who could start Saturday. Illinois has a freshman who's never started before
item.description: The Oregon Ducks will face a team on Saturday with an even less desirable quarterback situation. Illinois (3-3, 1-2 Big Ten) quarterback Katin Houser suffered a broken hand that will sideline him for four to six weeks during a 38-37 overtime win over Michigan State on Oct. 10. Oregon has played its last two games without starting quarterback Dante Moore, who suffered a concussion in the second quarter of the Ducks’ 41-27 win at USC on Sept. 26. However, while Oregon can turn to junior Dylan Raiola — a Nebraska transfer with 23 career starts — and senior Brock Thomas, Illinois is relying on freshman quarterback Michael Clayton II, who will make his first start against the Ducks. A positive for Illinois is that Houser was injured before the team’s bye week, giving coach Bret Bielema two weeks to prepare Clayton. “It was just good timing,” Bielema told reporters during his Monday media session. Illinois is off to a disappointing start after going 9-4 in 2025 and 10-3 in 2024. The defense is below average, while the passing combination of Houser and wide receiver Collin Dixon is one of the nation’s best. Dixon is tied for third nationally with nine touchdown receptions. Illinois head coach Bret Bielema celebrates their overtime win over Michigan State as he walks off the field after an NCAA college football game, Saturday, Oct. 10, 2026, in East Lansing, Mich. (AP Photo/Lon Horwedel) AP Photo/Lon Horwedel AP Photo/Lon Horwedel Now Illinois heads into Saturday’s game against a resurgent Oregon defense, trying to get Clayton up to speed. His performance against MSU elevated expectations. Houser left the game late in the third quarter with Illinois leading 23-10. Clayton completed 6 of 8 passes for 88 yards and two touchdowns. The final touchdown came in overtime on a 25-yard pass that put Illinois up 38-31. Sophomore quarterback Carson Boyd also played. He rushed once for seven yards but did not attempt a pass. Bielema and offensive coordinator Barry Lunney Jr. both said Boyd could play against Oregon (4-2, 2-1), but Clayton is the starter. Usually, Bielema said, his starting quarterback gets a lot of rest during the bye week while the staff works on player development. Given Clayton and Boyd’s inexperience, both got valuable reps in practice last week. “I think those two guys in particular took advantage of every rep,” Bielema said. Bielema has leaned heavily on transfer quarterbacks during his six years at Illinois, including Houser. But that could change if Clayton, a former three-star recruit, earns the job. “I’ve said several times that hopefully the next starter comes from within our program,” Bielema said. Lunney said Clayton will be more prepared than he has in the past given the circumstances. Michigan State Spartans defensive back Charles Brantley (4) tackles Illinois Fighting Illini wide receiver Collin Dixon (17) in a Big 10 football game at Spartan Stadium in East Lansing, Mich. on Saturday, October 10, 2026. Isaac Ritchey | iritchey@mlive

item.title: Reeling Oregon Ducks remain positive, committed to the grind
item.description: EUGENE — The 2026 season is on the verge of completely unraveling for the Oregon Ducks . One more loss, and any shred of postseason hopes would be extinguished. Yet even after two upset losses and falling out of the rankings — despite starting the season at No. 2 — the Ducks (3-2, 1-1 Big Ten) remain focused, together and committed to salvaging the season. “One thing I really love is the way the people in the locker room have been responding to this adversity,” sophomore cornerback Brandon Finney Jr. said. After his team’s 17-15 loss to No. 12 UCLA on Saturday, Oregon coach Dan Lanning said the team would be measured by how it responds moving forward. On Wednesday, he said the team has elevated its work ethic and embraced accountability. “I’ve been proud of the way that they’ve worked,” Lanning said. “I don’t see a lot of hanging heads, right? I think that’s challenging, too, especially when you’re young, to not lose a little bit of gusto and not lose a little bit of belief.” Oregon linebacker Devon Jackson (#9) drops UCLA running back Wayne Knight (#3) for no gain as the No. 13 Ducks face the No. 21 Bruins in a Big Ten college football game at Autzen Stadium in Eugene on Saturday, Oct. 10, 2026. Sean Meagher/The Oregonian The Ducks, who host Nebraska (5-1, 2-1) at 8 p.m. Saturday, responded well to adversity following a 39-31 loss at Oklahoma State on Sept. 12. Oregon won its next two games, including a 41-27 win at USC on Sept. 26. That victory seemed to give the Ducks a fresh start. But two weeks later, they lost to the Bruins and dropped out of the rankings. Now, Oregon must run the table to have a legitimate shot at the College Football Playoff, which seemed like a given for a team that returned most of its starters from last year’s semifinal squad. RELATED : Can the Ducks bounce back from UCLA loss? Experts release new Oregon vs. Nebraska predictions It’s not uncommon for teams with grand expectations to unravel in tough times. So far, that hasn’t happened. “The team is very connected and maintains its composure whether we’re winning or losing,” punter Bailey Ettridge said. “We haven’t let the losses last week and against Oklahoma State bring us down. I think we’ve handled them well.” Wide receiver Dakorien Moore said the team is filled with players who came to Oregon to win and be great. He added that the team’s goals remain attainable, and team leaders have worked to encourage togetherness and mutual trust. “If you can’t trust your teammate, then everything ain’t going to form in the way that it’s supposed to,” he said. This also means trusting the process, the plan and the team’s goal to get better instead of blaming one another. Oregon head coach Dan Lanning talks to the defense during a timeout as the No. 13 Oregon Ducks face the No. 21 UCLA Bruins in a Big Ten college football game at Autzen Stadium in Eugene on Saturday, Oct. 10, 2026. item.title: 10 takeaways from Oregon’s loss at Illinois and firing of OC Drew Mehringer
item.description: CHAMPAIGN, Ill. — The Oregon Ducks (4-3, 2-2 Big Ten) suffered their worst loss of the season at Illinois on Saturday . The 21-10 defeat came against a marginal Illinois team that started a true freshman at quarterback, rushed for 225 yards, and held Oregon to two scoring drives. As a result, on Sunday, Oregon coach Dan Lanning announced the firing of offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer . What that means for the rest of the season remains to be seen. Mehringer had to contend with several key personnel issues, including starting quarterback Dante Moore missing three games while in concussion protocol. Here are 10 takeaways from Saturday’s game and the firing of Mehringer: 1. It feels like Mehringer is the scapegoat in this mess Criticizing play-calling is an armchair quarterback’s delight, but doing so under Oregon’s current circumstances is somewhat obtuse. Few teams excel without their starting quarterback. The next factor is an offensive line that was clearly mismanaged in the offseason after losing three starters to the NFL. Next is inconsistent play from backup quarterbacks Dylan Raiola and Brock Thomas. Then sprinkle in losing top wideout Jeremiah McClellan (broken foot) after three games, starting wide receiver Evan Stewart (undisclosed injury) for the last two games, and two more rotational wide receivers heading into Illinois. Does all of that excuse Mehringer for Oregon scoring just 42 points over the past three weeks? No. But those are a lot of obstacles for any offensive coordinator to overcome. Watch " Oregon football fires offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer " on YouTube Watch 2. Where does Lanning go from here? Lanning will probably announce his new offensive coordinator during his Monday press conference. He could promote from within to get through the season and then conduct a national search in the offseason. Or he may have someone in mind to take over now and beyond. Whatever Lanning decides, the next play-caller had better hope Moore returns, or little will change. 3. It could be time to add a veteran coach to the staff Lanning did well by hiring younger offensive coordinators, Kenny Dillingham and then Will Stein. But maybe it’s time to bring in an accomplished, seasoned veteran coach to add a new perspective to a relatively young staff. Someone with a track record of success as an offensive coordinator and maybe as a head coach. Someone like former Oregon coach Chip Kelly, Northwestern’s offensive coordinator. No, don’t expect Kelly to want to return to Oregon. But someone like him could fit perfectly. 4. The wide receiver situation After Saturday’s game, Raiola was asked twice how difficult it was to build timing with the receiving crew, which lacked McClellan, Stewart, and freshmen Messiah Hampton and Jalen Lott. item.title: Oregon QB Dante Moore ruled out for rest of 2026 season
item.description: Oregon Ducks quarterback Dante Moore will miss the rest of the season, coach Dan Lanning announced Monday night. “I’m not anticipating him being back this season,” Lanning said. “Really got clarity for us this past week, for him,” Lanning added. “And I think if it were up to Dante in any shape, way, he would want to be out there playing for the guys. But, unfortunately, it’s not really up to Dante. It’s not really up to me. We can control the setting and practice where he’s able to do things for us, but that’s not always the case in the game.” Lanning said he expects Moore, who has run scout-team offense in practice, to fully recover. “That hasn’t changed,” Lanning said. “Definitely feel that way, but for him to be out there on the field for us right now, that’s not gonna happen.” Lanning added that Moore would remain involved with the team. “He’s still going to be a big part of this team and helping us move forward and find opportunities for us to be better,” Lanning said. Watch " Oregon Ducks QB Dante Moore to miss remainder of 2026 season " on YouTube Watch The announcement comes days after the reeling Ducks lost 21-10 at Illinois on Saturday in the third straight game Moore missed while in concussion protocol. Before the Illinois game, Moore told The Oregonian/OregonLive that he felt good but didn’t know if he’d return this season and was taking it “one day at a time.” “That’s all I can do,” he said. He then began throwing passes on the field in shorts and a sweatshirt. Saturday’s loss all but knocked Oregon (4-3, 2-2 Big Ten) out of the national playoff picture and led Lanning to fire offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer on Sunday. Without Moore, Oregon scored 42 points over three games and lost twice while rotating between backup quarterbacks Dylan Raiola and Brock Thomas. Moore was injured on Sept. 26 at USC while sliding to end a 10-yard run to the USC 13-yard line. As Moore began to slide, Trojans linebacker Desman Stephens II hit him in the head with his shoulder. Oregon quarterback Dante Moore, center bottom, takes a hard tackle by lSouthern California inebacker Desman Stephens II, center top, during the first half of an NCAA college football game, Saturday, Sept. 26, 2026, in Los Angeles. (AP Photo/Mark J. Terrill) AP Photo/Mark J. Terrill Moore was taken off the field in a cart and loaded into an ambulance. Following Moore’s injury, Raiola entered the game and led the Ducks to a 41-27 win. Moore entered the concussion protocol but returned to practice the following bye week. Speculation was that Moore would return once he cleared the protocols. But each subsequent availability report listed Moore as out. On Oct. 10, Oregon lost 17-15 to UCLA, with Raiola struggling through three quarters before being replaced in the fourth quarter by Thomas. item.title: Dame Time is back in Portland — and the Blazers look dangerous
item.description: A new head coach will roam the sidelines. A franchise icon will make his long-awaited return. An All-Star will begin his redemption tour. And a new ownership group will watch its first season opener from Paul Allen’s former seats along the Moda Center baseline. The Blazers open the 2026-27 NBA season Wednesday night against the Phoenix Suns — a team they upset in April in the play-in tournament — and if you’re just now tuning in for the start of the regular season, well, there’s a lot you missed. RELATED: Suns vs. Blazers predictions, odds and best bets: Dame is home, and the model likes Portland on opening night Let’s catch you up. What does the starting lineup look like? The Blazers are expected to unveil a new starting lineup that features a pair of notable All-Star additions: Damian Lillard and Ja Morant . The backcourt duo is joining a fivesome that includes returning starters Deni Avdija , Toumani Camara and Donovan Clingan . It’s a versatile, star-studded lineup that features three All-Stars, a former All-Defensive Second Team selection, one of the best young centers in the NBA and loads of scoring potential. What about the rotation? Micah Nori , the Blazers’ first-year head coach, said he plans on using a 10-man rotation to start the season, which will allow the Blazers to capitalize on their depth and versatility. In addition to the starters, Jrue Holiday, Scoot Henderson, Sidy Cissoko, Robert Williams III and Vit Krejci are expected to open the season in the rotation. The group could change depending on matchups and Williams’ availability — he did not play in back-to-backs last season — and it’s likely that Micah Potter, Branden Carlson and Yang Hansen will occasionally see spot duty, as well. Wait … the Blazers have a new coach? The Blazers stabilized their turbulent coaching situation in June, hiring longtime NBA assistant Nori to replace interim coach Tiago Splitter . Nori, who interviewed for head coaching jobs seven times before finally landing his first chance, is entering his 29th season in the league and is universally revered in NBA circles for his positive approach, ability to connect with players and sharp basketball mind. Early indications have been encouraging, as the Blazers players seem to love him and the front office works well with him. The Blazers’ coaching position had been embroiled in controversy, of course, as former coach Chauncey Billups — who was placed on indefinite leave by the NBA — is facing federal felony charges related to money laundering and wire fraud conspiracy for his alleged involvement in a rigged underground poker game. What style will the Blazers play? In a stark contrast to recent seasons, the Blazers are constructed around their offense rather than their defense. The roster is unbalanced, featuring five dynamic ball-handlers and playmakers (Lillard, Morant, Avdija, Holiday and Henderson), a solid center combination (Clingan and Williams) and little wing depth. item.title: OSU's Legree leads nation in receiving as WSU clash looms
item.description: CORVALLIS — There may be no more appropriate way to describe Oregon State’s outrageously successful passing game this season than explosive. The Beavers lead the country in passing yards thanks in large part to 10 passes of 40-plus yards. Jesse Legree is responsible for eight of those catches, including all five of OSU’s 50-yard pass plays this season, making it no surprise that he leads the country in receiving yards and touchdowns entering this week’s matchup with Washington State. “You see him with ball in space, obviously taking the top off a number of times,” Washington State coach Kirby Moore said. “I think it’s about playing team defense. Obviously communication is going to be really important, where he’s at.” The Cougars (1-5, 0-2 Pac-12) have the No. 2 defense in the Pac-12 thus far and are having that success by keeping the top on their pass coverage. WSU has allowed 11 passes of 30-plus yards, which is tied for 129th nationally and nearly 10% of the passes it has allowed. However, opponents are not breaking through that mark often, with just four passes over 40 yards and none for more than 50, one of 30 teams yet to allow such a play this season. “We don’t want to let the verticals up,” Washington State safety Jaylen Smith said. “We take pride in (not) letting deep balls go. We always look to play top down and take away the deep routes first.” WSU defensive coordinator Trent Bray will be tasked with doing what nobody has been able to do yet this season: contain Legree. OSU offensive coordinator Mitch Dahlen has been creative in moving Legree around to prevent defenses from taking him away. Last week against San Diego State that included moving Legree into the backfield for a variety of plays. “People are going to try and hit him at the line of scrimmage,” Dahlen said. “They’re going to try and two-hand jam. If they’re going to try and two-hand jam, it’s like OK, how can I move this guy enough where you can’t do that? You put him in the backfield, unless you want to jump offsides and do it, you can’t do it that way. “That’s what we do a good job of as a staff, is moving him around where you can’t just put a safety over the top of him because if he’s in the backfield, what are you going to do there?” Even if the Cougars manage to limit Legree, the Beavers have shown they are more than capable of going elsewhere, with an outrageous 14 players catching passes last week. Aeryn Hampton (20 receptions for 245 yards) and tight ends Eric Olsen and DeCorion Temple each have at least 20 catches and Aaron Butler has four grabs for at least 20 yards. item.title: Jaji wins Zamfara APC rerun primary with 26,646 votes
item.description: By Musa Ubandawaki, Sokoto The incumbent member representing Kaura Namoda/Birnin Magaji Federal Constituency of Zamfara State in the House of Representatives, Hon. Aminu Sani Jaji, has won the All Progressives Congress (APC) court-ordered fresh primary election with 26,646 votes. Jaji defeated two other aspirants in the rerun conducted on Wednesday, November 11, 2026, to reclaim the party’s ticket after his earlier nomination was nullified by the Federal High Court in Abuja. The Chairman of the APC Electoral Committee for the exercise, Hon. Kabiru Idris, announced the results at the Kaura Namoda Collation Centre after the conclusion of voting and collation across the two local government areas. According to the committee, the constituency had 42,266 registered APC members, out of whom 27,389 were accredited, while 27,359 votes were recorded as total votes cast. Jaji’s closest challenger, Hassan Umar Dangaladima, polled 713 votes, while the third contestant, Musa Zubairu, failed to secure any vote. A breakdown of the results showed that Jaji won in both local government areas, polling 14,264 votes in Kaura Namoda against Dangaladima’s 465, while Zubairu scored zero. In Birnin Magaji, Jaji secured 12,382 votes, compared with Dangaladima’s 248 votes, while Zubairu again failed to record any vote. Declaring the results, Idris said Jaji had satisfied the requirements of the law, the APC Constitution and the party’s guidelines governing primary elections. “Having satisfied the requirements of the law, the APC Constitution and guidelines, I hereby declare Hon. Aminu Sani Jaji the winner of the fresh primary election,” he announced. The rerun followed a legal challenge instituted by Dangaladima at the Federal High Court in Abuja against Jaji’s earlier emergence as the party’s candidate for the constituency. The court nullified the earlier nomination and directed the APC to conduct a fresh primary within two weeks. The party’s national leadership subsequently fixed November 11, 2026, for the exercise in compliance with the court’s directive. Jaji, who is associated with the political camp of the Minister of State for Defence, Bello Matawalle, has now secured the party’s ticket through the court-ordered process. The outcome settles the party’s immediate nomination contest in the constituency ahead of the 2027 general elections, following the legal dispute over its earlier primary election. item.title: Robinhood’s Crypto Trading Volume Falls 48% in October as Event Contracts More Than Double
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Robinhood’s Crypto Trading Volume Falls 48% in October as Event Contracts More Than Double Crypto trading on Robinhood fell by almost half from a year ago in October, the company said Thursday , as customers traded $17 billion of digital assets while their bets on event contracts more than doubled. The $17 billion figure was down 21% from September and 48% from October 2025, when crypto notional volume reached $32.5 billion. It covers both the flagship Robinhood app and Bitstamp, the crypto exchange the company bought in 2025. Volume in the Robinhood app fell to $6.8 billion, down 24% from September and 51% from a year earlier. Bitstamp handled $10.2 billion, down 18% month over month and 45% year over year. Average daily crypto volume across both platforms came to $548 million, compared with $713 million in September and about $1.05 billion a year ago. Daily average crypto trades slipped to about 700,000 from 900,000 in September and 1.1 million in October 2025. Event contracts take off as crypto cools The contrast with Robinhood’s prediction markets business is stark. Customers traded 5.9 billion event contracts in October, up 5% from September and 136% from the 2.5 billion traded a year earlier. Average daily volume reached 190 million contracts. Robinhood counts crypto and prediction markets on the same 31-day calendar, since both trade every day, so the comparison is apples to apples. Event contracts let users bet on outcomes such as elections, sports and economic data, and October’s tally covered the final weeks before the Nov. 3 midterm elections. That growth has drawn scrutiny in Washington. Sen. Elizabeth Warren, who is set to chair the Senate Banking Committee in January, plans to crack down on prediction markets and election betting platforms. The rest of Robinhood’s brokerage held up better than crypto. Equity notional volume rose 2% from a year earlier to $325 billion, and options contracts traded climbed 8% to 289 million. Margin balances reached $22.9 billion, up 39% year over year. Funded customers rose by about 130,000 in the month to 28.9 million, and net deposits came to $15.1 billion. Total platform assets slipped 3% from September to $383 billion but were up 12% from a year earlier. Robinhood did not say why crypto activity fell. The release, like all of the company’s monthly updates, is unaudited and preliminary. Retail pulls back as bitcoin slides The slump in Robinhood’s crypto numbers lines up with a broader retreat by retail traders. Bitcoin ended September near $83,500 and has slid since, falling below $70,000 early Friday for the first time since August as a hot inflation report raised bets on a Federal Reserve rate hike in December. Institutional demand has cooled alongside it. U.S. spot bitcoin exchange-traded funds posted a sixth straight day of net outflows on Thursday, and BlackRock’s IBIT, the largest of them, bled about $2 billion over nine sessions through Wednesday. The official line-up also includes Benjamin Fredrick, Ola Aina, Abdullahi Bewene, Wilfred Ndidi, Alhassan Yusuf, Tochukwu Nnadi, Alex Iwobi and Akor Adams. Nigeria’s expected starting XI vs Tanzania Stanley Nwabali Calvin Bassey Benjamin Fredrick Ola Aina Abdullahi Bewene Wilfred Ndidi Alhassan Yusuf Tochukwu Nnadi Alex Iwobi Ademola Lookman Akor Adams Head coach Éric Chelle will be looking to guide Nigeria to victory as the three-time African champions seek to strengthen their chances of qualifying for the tournament. item.title: Microsoft’s massive Outlook outage continues

item.title: Another Linux kernel developer steps back from some duties due to overload
item.description: Arm's Lorenzo Stoakes isn't quitting Linux kernel development, though he's stepping back from some of the patch-review work he used to handle. Stoakes is a principal software engineer at Arm and he's a busy chap. Aside from writing the forthcoming book The Linux Memory Manager , in his CV [PDF], he says: "I hold four maintainerships: memory mapping, memory mapping (locking), memory mapping (madvise) – essentially the entirety of the userland API to memory management – and the reverse mapping which connects physical to virtual memory." Even so, he plans to soon be doing a little less. Earlier this week he posted an email to the Linux kernel mailing list to say that he was planning to drop some of his workload. He explained: "Given the current throughput in the kernel resulting from AI-generated series, I unfortunately lack the bandwidth to generally be able to offer review except in those areas I maintain. […] Apologies for doing this, but given the current trends I'd like to do something to make my inbox a little more manageable." As it happens, this came just the day after the Paramount Penguin himself said that he saw signs that the AI patch tide was "starting to turn." Stoakes told The Register : "I am retaining my maintainerships and have no plans on giving those up, I just want my inbox to be less horrendous. "And yeah, AI is part of the reason; in general, it's gone from 'once a week' to 'daily' to 'half of what I see in review'. "But the AI wave is hitting [memory management] across the board, really." He added: "I have a habit of burning myself out over weekends and evenings – you can see my involvement on a thread talking about that here - which gives you a sense of my views if you read back through that thread." At the Open Source Summit last month, the Reg FOSS desk joined the "Ask the Expert" session with Greg Kroah-Hartman , and he too expressed worrying sentiments: "The onslaught of the LLM-generated patches… we don't have enough people to review them all… We need more reviewers. We don't have enough. All of the maintainers are burnt out, and we have been for ten years." Kroah-Hartman also said: "I want to go down to two Long Term Support releases – four, maximum. Six is too many. We're too busy. We don't have the manpower. It’s crazy." On Red Hat's model of offering 10 years of support for products with a given version of the kernel: "Debian does it right. Debian and Yocto run the world. I've argued for years that the RHEL and SLES model is broken. That's why I don't work for SUSE any more." ®

item.title: Malaysia arrests 53 Nigerians over immigration offences
item.description: By Favour Ulebor & Agency Report No fewer than 53 Nigerians were among 112 undocumented African nationals arrested by Malaysian immigration authorities between January and October 31 over various immigration offences, Malaysian newspaper, Utusan Malaysia, has reported. The Nigerians recorded the highest number of arrests among the African nationals, followed by Uganda with 13, Kenya with 10 and Ghana with eight. The Director-General of Malaysia’s Immigration Department, Datuk Zakaria Shaaban, disclosed the figures in an interview with Utusan Malaysia, published on Friday. According to the report, other nationals arrested included Somalia (6), Tanzania (6), Senegal (4), Algeria (3), Burkina Faso (2), Togo (2) and The Gambia (2). One national each from Guinea, Zimbabwe and Libya was also arrested. Shaaban said the most common offence was entering or remaining in Malaysia without a valid pass or permit, contrary to Section 6(1)(c) of the Immigration Act 1959/63. He said 85 people were arrested for the offence, including 47 Nigerians. “The primary offence recorded is entering and remaining in the country without a valid pass or permit, under Section 6(1)(c) of the Immigration Act 1959/63; this resulted in 85 arrests, 47 of which involved Nigerian nationals,” he said. The immigration chief said 23 others were arrested for overstaying their permitted period under Section 15(1)(c) of the same Act. He added that three people were detained for violating the conditions of their immigration passes under Regulation 39(b) of the Immigration Regulations 1963. One Nigerian was also arrested for allegedly possessing forged documents under Section 56(1)(l) of the Immigration Act. The authorities also arrested an Algerian employer under Section 55B of the Act for allegedly employing foreign workers without valid immigration passes. Shaaban said the enforcement operations were part of efforts to curb undocumented migration and prosecute employers who engage or accommodate foreign nationals without proper immigration documents. “These ongoing enforcement operations reflect the authorities’ steadfast commitment to curbing the presence of undocumented migrants and taking firm action against any employers who harbor or employ them,” he said. However, the report did not disclose the identities of the Nigerians arrested or the specific locations where the arrests were made. The post Malaysia arrests 53 Nigerians over immigration offences appeared first on Vanguard News .
