item.title: 2027: Wike Criticises Obi Over National Anthem Snub At NDC Lagos Town Hall Meeting
item.description: The Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nyesom Wike, has said that the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, demonstrated lawlessness and an intent to divide Nigeria by allegedly refusing to recite the official one. Wike made these remarks on Friday, during a stakeholders’ town hall meeting in Ogu-Bolo Local Government Area of Rivers State, organised under the banner of the Rainbow Coalition to mobilise support for President Bola Tinubu’s 2027 re-election bid and All Progressives Congress (APC) candidates. ﻿ Addressing traditional rulers, community leaders, youths, and party faithful, the FCT minister argued that a leader who disregards national symbols cannot be trusted with the presidency. “A whole national anthem of a country is being sung. A man who wants to be President of Nigeria would disobey and sit down. And then not only that, when a different national anthem that is not being used for Nigeria [was sung], he stood up. “In a way, he does not belong to this country. In a way, he has said he does not belong to this country; that if you give him the president, he would do a different thing that will divide Nigeria. “A man who does not believe in Nigeria, someone who derives joy in ridiculing the country by disrespecting its symbolic National Anthem must not be allowed to come near the presidency of our country,” the minister said. Wike further criticised Obi’s political trajectory and past governance record, alleging that the former Anambra State governor frequently abandons political parties whenever internal crises arise, rather than staying to resolve them. He also faulted Obi for not conducting local government elections during his eight-year tenure as governor, describing it as a contradiction to his professed belief in the rule of law. Tackles Atiku, Amaechi In addition to targeting Obi, the FCT Minister took aim at the opposition coalition involving former Vice President Atiku Abubakar and former Rivers State Governor Rotimi Amaechi. Wike questioned their track records in public office, specifically citing the state of seaports during Amaechi’s tenure as Minister of Transportation and alleging that the administration demolished Government Secondary School, Ogu, without rebuilding it, alongside unfulfilled promises regarding a 1,000-bed specialist hospital. Urging the people of Ogu-Bolo to disregard what he termed “big grammar” from opposition politicians on television, Wike maintained that President Bola Tinubu’s administration had delivered tangible dividends of democracy to the area. He pointed to the construction of the Ogu-Bolo Civic Centre—facilitated through the federal appointment of an indigene, Boma Iyaye—as well as the conduct of local government elections. He urged people in the area to massively support the re-election of Tinubu, Kingsley Chinda for Governor of Rivers State and all the APC candidates seeking National Assembly seats. item.title: It's the end of the world as we know it, per a physicist's 1960 prediction
item.description: As of this morning, Microsoft is still scrambling to restore service following yesterday's global outage, with millions of users unable to access Outlook and other vital tools. It's not the end of the world, but it does seem fitting that this should happen on the day a physicist predicted would be the end of humanity: November 13, 2026. And it falls on a Friday, too. The physicist in question is Heinz von Foerster, who published a 1960 paper in the journal Science predicting that by today, overpopulation would reach the breaking point. It's not a new fear. English economist Thomas Malthus —one of the early pioneers in modeling population dynamics—made a similar prediction in 1798, claiming that a rapidly growing population would eventually exhaust the available food supply, and humanity would starve to death. His model rested on the assumption of exponential growth, but the equation is only applicable under specific conditions, such as scientists growing bacteria in a lab in a perfectly controlled environment. Even then, while growth occurs exponentially for a time, it does not continue forever. Population dynamics are notoriously tricky to calculate because there are so many variables to consider and so much unpredictability in the system. In his 1960 analysis, Von Foerster accurately measured past trends in population growth, but like Malthus, he assumed those trends would carry into the future largely unchanged. So he projected that human population growth would march inexorably toward infinity. We wouldn't starve to death; von Foerster thought we would be ingenious enough to solve the food supply problem. Instead, "they will be squeezed to death," he wrote. Read full article Comments

item.title: 10 footballers with the most red cards in football history
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Footballers are often praised for keeping their cool when the stakes are high, but some of the game’s most recognisable names have become known for receiving repeated red cards. From tough-tackling defenders to forceful midfielders, their careers have combined success on the pitch with frequent disciplinary woes. Gerardo Bedoya stands clear at the top of the ranking, with 46 red cards during his playing career and recognised by the Guinness World Records. The former Colombia international’s fiery reputation followed him into coaching: in 2016, he was sent off just 21 minutes into his first match as an assistant coach at Santa Fe. Red-card totals can differ between databases because no single global record tracks every player’s dismissals across all competitions. According to a recent ranking by Planet Football, here are the 10 players who have been sent off the most times in football history. Alexis Ruano Delgado — 22 red cards The Spanish centre-back played for Málaga, Getafe, Valencia and Sevilla, among other clubs. He won the Copa del Rey with Valencia in 2008. Rafael Márquez — 22 red cards The Mexican defender played for Barcelona, Monaco and New York Red Bulls, among other clubs, and represented Mexico at five World Cups. Six of his red cards came during his time at Barcelona. Cyril Rool — 22 red cards The French midfielder played in Ligue 1 for clubs including Lens, Bordeaux and Nice. His career, which ran from 1993 to 2010, also included more than 150 yellow cards. Gerardo Torrado — 22 red cards Mexico’s former defensive midfielder earned 144 international caps and played at three World Cups. He spent 11 years at Cruz Azul, where he was sent off 14 times. Paolo Montero — 23 red cards The Uruguayan defender played for Atalanta and Juventus, winning Serie A titles with the Turin club. Sixteen of his 23 dismissals came in Italy’s top flight, where he holds the league record, according to the ranking. Edgar Davids — 25 red cards The Dutch midfielder won the Champions League with Ajax and also played for Juventus and Tottenham. Known for his energetic style, he continued his career with Barnet in England’s lower leagues. Felipe Melo — 26 red cards The Brazilian midfielder and defender played for clubs including Juventus, Inter, Galatasaray, Palmeiras and Fluminense. He retired in 2024, aged 41, after a career spanning more than two decades. Pablo Alfaro — 27 red cards The Spanish centre-back played for Barcelona, Atlético Madrid, Racing Santander and Sevilla. He was part of Barcelona’s 1992–93 La Liga-winning squad and later earned a UEFA Cup winner’s medal with Sevilla. Sergio Ramos — 30 red cards The World Cup winner and former Real Madrid captain is second, with 30 career dismissals. His total includes 26 red cards at Real Madrid and four across spells with Sevilla, Paris Saint-Germain and Monterrey. item.title: NIS moves to prevent foreign interference in 2027 elections
item.description: The Nigeria Immigration Service (NIS) and other stakeholders have convened to strategise measures to prevent interference by foreign elements in the upcoming 2027 general elections. The NIS, the Department of State Services (DSS), the Border Communities Development Agency (BCDA) and other stakeholders convened at a sensitisation workshop at the NIS headquarters on Friday in Abuja. The workshop is themed: “The Role of the Nigeria Immigration Service in Election Monitoring and Management.” Speaking at the workshop, the NIS Comptroller-General, Mrs Kemi Nandap, said that the successful conduct of the upcoming elections required institutional cooperation from all security stakeholders. Nandap, represented by the Deputy Comptroller-General in charge of Visa and Residency, Mrs Franca Nwanneka, said that the deliberation was important as the general election is fast approaching. “Beyond the responsibility of conducting credible elections, there is the equally important task of providing a peaceful and secure environment in which the democratic process can thrive. “Achieving this requires collective vigilance, effective coordination and the commitment of all institutions entrusted with safeguarding our nation,” she said. According to her, the NIS occupied a strategic position in the nation’s security architecture as the agency saddled with the responsibility and mandate of border security and migration management. “We must therefore remain alert to the influx of foreigners, emerging threats, particularly irregular migration and smuggling of migrants. “We must also be on high alert to trafficking in persons and other transnational criminal activities capable of undermining national security,” she said. Nandap also reaffirmed the NIS’ stance as a non-partisan service loyal to the Constitution and the Federal Republic of Nigeria, and warned officers against using official capabilities to participate in politics. She charged officers to demonstrate the highest standards of political neutrality, discipline and respect for the rule of law. The CG charged senior officers, zonal coordinators, comptrollers, and heads of formations to ensure that every command is adequately prepared before, during and after the elections. She emphasised strengthened surveillance, intelligence gathering, effective deployment and close coordination with relevant security agencies as key areas that could facilitate credible elections. “No single agency can address the complex security challenges confronting our nation in isolation. Our collective strength lies in our ability to work together, share timely information and respond decisively to emerging threats. “I look forward to even stronger collaboration as we approach the elections because the task of securing our nation and sustaining public confidence in our institutions is a collective responsibility,” she added. item.title: Astronaut Suni Williams rides through NYC as Grand Marshal of the Veterans Day Parade | Space photo of the day for Nov. 13, 2026
item.description: null NASA astronaut Suni Williams rides through New York City as the Grand Marshal of the Veterans Day Parade on Nov. 11, 2026. (Image credit: Photo by Slaven Vlasic/Getty Images) New Yorkers got a space-y surprise on Wednesday (Nov. 11): Retired NASA astronaut and U.S. Navy Captain Sunita "Suni" Williams rolled down 5th Avenue in the back of a classic convertible wrapped in patriotic decals as Grand Marshal of the Veterans Day Parade. What is it? On Wednesday, New York City's 107th annual Veterans Day Parade made its way through Manhattan to the cheers and respectful nods of thousands of onlookers. The parade is an annual tradition on the holiday, which honors veterans of the U.S. armed forces. As part of the parade, veterans, active-duty soldiers, firefighters, marching bands, youth cadets and more march through the city and honor those who have served and sacrificed in the U.S. military. This year, the parade featured Suni Williams as its grand marshal. "I’m proud to join New Yorkers and Americans from around the country in honoring the service, sacrifice, and commitment of veterans from every generation," she said during the event. Why is it incredible? Williams was selected for NASA's astronaut program in 1998 and retired from it in December 2025 . She spent 608 days in space during her astronaut career, the second-most by an American astronaut behind Peggy Whitson , who racked up 695. Williams also had an extensive career in the U.S. Navy. She began as an ensign in 1987 before serving in a number of different roles. For example, she was a diving officer and a naval aviator and also provided helicopter combat support during Operation Desert Shield and Operation Provide Comfort. She further served as a squadron safety officer and finally as a captain, a rank she achieved in 2017. During this time, Williams supported relief efforts following Hurricane Andrew, trained within the U.S. Naval Test Pilot School and gained a wealth of further experience flying as a military pilot. Williams is part of a longstanding tradition of astronauts serving in the U.S. military. From test pilots to naval officers and more, there's a strong link between the U.S. armed forces and NASA's astronaut program.

item.title: I saw Saturn’s rings in seconds with the Celestron StarSense Explorer 150mm Tabletop Dobsonian telescope — full review
item.description: null Saturn was only a night past its annual opposition when I pointed the Celestron StarSense Explorer 150mm Tabletop Dobsonian straight at it. The planet was at its biggest and brightest of the year, the seeing was good and its famous rings were visibly opening up after appearing edge-on from Earth in recent years. It was an obvious target for a new telescope. Finding it took seconds. After selecting Saturn in Celestron’s StarSense Explorer app, I followed the on-screen arrows as I moved the telescope across the sky. As I got closer, the app zoomed in until a bullseye turned green. I looked through the supplied 25mm eyepiece, then swapped to the 10mm to see a pale yellow Saturn at 75x magnification, with its rings sharply defined and its giant moon Titan visible in orbit. At 25 lbs (11.33 kg), the Celestron StarSense Explorer 150mm Tabletop Dobsonian is a relative heavyweight. Jamie Carter The supplied 25mm and 10mm Kellner eyepieces provide 30x and 75x magnification, respectively, but are obvious candidates for future upgrades. Jamie Carter The StarSense Explorer smartphone dock uses a small mirror. Jamie Carter It was a stunning view, and exactly the kind of experience a beginner needs from a first telescope. There was no frustration and no wondering whether I was looking in the right place. StarSense took me straight there — but, crucially, I moved the telescope myself. I’ve always liked that combination of hand-holding and DIY observing that Celestron’s StarSense tech gives you. I’m less convinced by the tabletop telescope it’s attached to. Although this $599 RRP (£379) model is significantly smaller than the Celestron StarSense Explorer 8-inch Dobsonian telescope I’ve previously reviewed, it still weighs 25 lbs (11.33 kg). You need to place it on something sturdy before you can use it comfortably. After living with it in my backyard, I’m not convinced the tabletop format is the advantage it initially appears to be. An iPhone 16 Pro Max fitted securely into the StarSense Explorer smartphone dock during testing. (Image credit: Jamie Carter) What StarSense Explorer does well The Celestron StarSense Explorer 150mm Tabletop Dobsonian comes with a red dot finder for manual navigation. (Image credit: Jamie Carter) I’ve used Celestron’s StarSense Explorer system on a variety of telescopes and have always been impressed by how easy this type of smartphone navigation is to use. The technology works just as well here and, for me, it remains one of the best ways of making a traditional optical telescope accessible to a complete beginner. This isn’t a computerized GoTo telescope. There are no motors to slew across the sky automatically and no tracking system to keep an object centered. Instead, a smartphone sits in a dock attached to the telescope, and its camera looks at the sky via a small mirror. item.title: 2027: Adebutu hails court ruling, says justice has prevailed
item.description: By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) governorship candidate in Ogun State for the 2027 election, Hon. Oladipupo Adebutu, has hailed the judgment of the Federal High Court, Abuja, directing the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to restore his name to the list of candidates for the forthcoming governorship election within 24 hours. Adebutu described the judgment, delivered by Justice Peter Lifu on Friday, as a victory for justice, the rule of law and democratic principles. Reacting to the ruling in a statement, the PDP chieftain declared: “Justice has prevailed! Relief is here!” He described the judgment as a significant development in the legal battle over his exclusion from INEC’s published list of candidates for the 2027 Ogun State governorship election. Adebutu said he had consistently maintained that his PDP membership, registration and emergence as the party’s governorship candidate were legitimate and in accordance with due process. “From the moment my name was omitted from INEC’s published list, I maintained that the facts surrounding my PDP membership, registration and the process that produced me as the party’s governorship candidate were clear,” he said. According to him, the party remained confident in the strength of its position and resolved to pursue the matter through the appropriate legal channels. He noted that the judgment had reaffirmed the importance of due process, stressing that political and electoral disputes should be determined on their merits rather than on speculation or premature conclusions. Adebutu expressed appreciation to the national leadership of the PDP, particularly Chief Nyesom Wike, whom he described as the party’s national leader, and its National Chairman, Hon. Abdulrahman Mohammed, for their support and confidence throughout the legal proceedings. He also thanked the Ogun State PDP leadership, party members, supporters and residents of the state for their solidarity during the period of uncertainty. “I am equally grateful to the Ogun State PDP leadership, our members, supporters and the good people of Ogun State who remained steadfast. Your patience, encouragement and confidence have been invaluable,” he stated. The governorship candidate also commended the judiciary for its role in upholding justice, emphasising that democratic institutions must remain independent and impartial, irrespective of political interests or affiliations. “Our democratic institutions must remain strong, independent and committed to upholding the law, regardless of political interests or affiliations,” he said. Welcoming the judgment, Adebutu said his focus remained on addressing the developmental challenges confronting Ogun State and engaging residents on practical solutions to improve their welfare. item.title: Carrick says ‘love never dies’ after Man Utd sacking
item.description: Michael Carrick wished Manchester United “nothing but success” 24 hours after he was sacked, reaffirming his enduring love for the club, who have already appointed Mauricio Pochettino as his replacement. Carrick impressed after taking over as interim boss following Ruben Amorim’s acrimonious exit in January, leading United to Champions League qualification. He was rewarded with a two-year permanent deal, but results have nose-dived in this campaign. The Red Devils are in the Premier League relegation zone after winning just one of their 10 league matches so far. The Old Trafford club named former Tottenham, Chelsea and Paris Saint-Germain boss Pochettino, currently USA head coach, as their new manager on Friday. Despite the downturn this season, Carrick remained popular with supporters in part for his role as a player in multiple triumphs under Alex Ferguson, who retired in 2013. The 45-year-old said his affection remained rock-solid. “I want nothing but success for Manchester United. This club has been such a big part of my life and that will never change,” Carrick wrote in an Instagram post. “I’ll always be proud to have played my part and I’ll always want the very best for it. “I’ll be right there with you from now on, watching from the sidelines, cheering the lads on.” The former England midfielder paid tribute to the fans, his coaching staff and United’s players. “I’ve had the immense privilege of leading Manchester United, the football club that I love,” he wrote. “There are very few who get to live that and feel it, and for that I’m incredibly grateful. With that comes huge responsibility, and to be at Manchester United, you need to understand exactly what that means. “It’s different to anywhere else. Ultimately, you need to push to be the best, but there is a culture, there are values and there are behaviours that you have to live by and respect, which have been built over a long period of time. “It’s a football club that is unique, with substance and history that cannot be ignored. This is what inspired me every single day.” Carrick described United’s fans as a “special, rare breed”. “We’ve had some great times this year and moments we’ll all remember,” he said. “The best thing about being in my position was seeing so many of you lose yourselves in the emotion of those moments, leaving the stadium desperate to come back again next time. “I just wanted to give you something back. That love never dies.” The post Carrick says ‘love never dies’ after Man Utd sacking appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: FG Signs Port Harcourt Airport Concession Agreement, Assures Workers’ Protection
item.description: The Federal Government has signed a concession agreement for the Jeremiah Obafemi Awolowo International Airport, Port Harcourt, with PH Airport Limited, following assurances from the concessionaire that the arrangement would not lead to job losses. The agreement was signed at the office of the Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, in Abuja, on Thursday. The Federal Government delegation was led by Keyamo, while PH Airport Limited was represented by its Group Managing Director, Eyo Asuquo. The signing followed a meeting between the minister and aviation union leaders to discuss the implications of the concession for airport workers. Speaking on behalf of the unions, Comrade Ben Nnabue said organised labour had approved the agreement after receiving assurances that no aviation worker would lose their job as a result of the arrangement. He said job security remained a major concern for the unions and that they were satisfied with the commitments made before endorsing the agreement. Photo of the Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, and the federal government delegation in Abuja, on Thursday. Also speaking, Asuquo highlighted Port Harcourt’s strategic importance in the Gulf of Guinea, describing the airport as a potential gateway for regional commerce, investment and connectivity. He said PH Airport Limited intended to improve the airport’s infrastructure and operational standards, adding that the concession would create more employment opportunities rather than result in job losses. According to him, the company’s vision extends beyond managing the facility to expanding airport-related activities, attracting investment and unlocking its economic potential. The Director-General of the Nigeria Civil Aviation Authority, Chris Najomo; Managing Director of the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria, Olubunmi Kuku; ministry directors and aviation union leaders attended the event. The concession agreement was subsequently signed by the concessionaire and relevant ministry officials, with Keyamo presiding over the ceremony. The Federal Government said the agreement was part of its broader efforts to attract private-sector investment and expertise into the development and management of Nigeria’s airport infrastructure. Under President Bola Tinubu’s administration, the Ministry of Aviation and Aerospace Development has pursued reforms aimed at modernising airports, improving operational efficiency and strengthening the aviation sector’s contribution to economic growth. The Port Harcourt airport concession is expected to improve the passenger experience, strengthen airport services, and attract investment to the facility. item.title: Obi condemns attack on NDC supporters in Lagos, urges peaceful defence of votes
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has condemned the attack on the party’s supporters at a town hall meeting in Lagos on Thursday, urging them to remain peaceful while defending their democratic rights. Obi made the call in a statement posted on his X handle on Friday, a day after suspected thugs disrupted the party’s gathering in Oregun, Lagos. He said he had been informed that a group of thugs mobilised to attack participants who arrived early for the meeting, noting that he had travelled to Lagos from Abuja to attend a commendation service for Chief Sir Okey Ezibe before proceeding to join supporters at the town hall meeting. “The political violence being enabled by certain political actors against our supporters is an ill wind that blows no one any good. Anarchy consumes everyone,” he said. “We will remain law-abiding, even in the face of extreme provocation.” Obi said the town hall meeting went ahead despite the disruption and participants raised concerns about reviving the economy, the high cost of living, corruption, insecurity, support for vulnerable citizens and the integrity of elections. He said the first responsibility of any government was to secure the country and unite its people around a shared purpose. He also pledged that his administration would pursue policies to reduce living costs, improve welfare and invest in healthcare and education. On the forthcoming elections, the former Anambra governor said protecting the integrity of the process was a shared responsibility, saying the NDC would deploy agents to polling units to observe and document voting, ward collation and the final declaration of results. “I encouraged our people to eschew violence while remaining peaceful, vigilant, and resolute in defending their democratic rights,” he said. Vanguard reported that suspected political thugs armed with cutlasses, cudgels and stones invaded the Oregun rally on Thursday, attacking supporters and injuring some participants, although Obi was not at the rally when the incident occurred. The post Obi condemns attack on NDC supporters in Lagos, urges peaceful defence of votes appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Screenless GPS: Slate Auto says, "Remember the road atlas"
item.description: Whether it's nostalgia or a sense that technology has gotten a bit too pervasive, there’s no denying that Slate Auto appears to be tuned into the particular moment. The startup has a simple pitch : an affordable electric truck with just the basics , leaving owners to DIY and BYOD for everything else, all for a sub-$25,000 starting price. Among the things Slate does without is an embedded infotainment system. The small digital display on the dashboard that shows your speed and range is also where the backup camera appears if you engage reverse, and there are two USB-C ports that provide power but not connectivity, and that’s that. But there is a solution to getting lost, and it's called “Screenless GPS.” Even though we don’t have a Slate truck to test it with, the OEM sent us a unit to review. That’s right, it’s a good old spiral-bound road atlas! “We believe you should use the devices you know and love,” Slate says, and it reckons that maps worked just fine for past generations, so they should still work now. Read full article Comments

item.title: President Trump Taps Two Democrats in Bipartisan Slate of SEC and CFTC Nominees as Both Agencies Run Short-Handed
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine President Trump Taps Two Democrats in Bipartisan Slate of SEC and CFTC Nominees as Both Agencies Run Short-Handed President Donald Trump sent the Senate four nominees for the Securities and Exchange Commission and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission on Thursday, his first picks for either agency in about a year and the first Democrats he has put forward for them. Former CFTC Commissioner Kristin Johnson, a Democrat, and Republican Steven Levine were nominated to the SEC. Republican Nathan Anonick and Democrat Matthew Rowland were nominated to the CFTC, Bloomberg Law reported. Each nominee needs Senate confirmation. The Senate Banking Committee will handle the SEC picks, while the Senate Agriculture Committee will take up the CFTC pair before any vote by the full chamber. Who the nominees are Levine was tapped for the SEC seat left by Hester Peirce, whose term expired, for a term running through June 5, 2030. He most recently served as general counsel and a senior adviser at the White House Council of Economic Advisers and previously worked at the SEC as counsel and deputy chief of staff to Commissioner Mark Uyeda. Peirce led the SEC’s Crypto Task Force and was one of the agency’s most vocal supporters of clearer crypto rules. Johnson would take the seat formerly held by Democrat Caroline Crenshaw, for a term ending June 5, 2029. She served as a CFTC commissioner until 2025 and is a former law school professor. During her time at the CFTC, she spoke often about digital assets, including custody and decentralized finance. Both CFTC nominees come from the Senate Agriculture Committee, which oversees the derivatives regulator. Anonick is legislative counsel to Chairman John Boozman and was a lead negotiator on the committee’s portion of the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act. He was nominated to the seat once held by former Chairman Rostin Behnam, for a term ending June 19, 2031. Rowland is a CFTC attorney detailed to the committee who also worked on the Clarity Act and the committee’s 2024 crypto bill. He previously served on Johnson’s staff at the CFTC, according to his LinkedIn profile. He would fill the remainder of former Commissioner Summer Mersinger’s term, which expires April 13, 2028. Both agencies can seat up to five commissioners, with no more than three from one party. The SEC currently has two, Chairman Paul Atkins and Commissioner Mark Uyeda. Chairman Mike Selig is the CFTC’s only sitting commissioner. Lame-duck timing and a Democratic Senate The timing puts the nominees in front of a Senate in its lame-duck session, weeks after Democrats swept both chambers of Congress in the Nov. 3 midterms. Sen. Elizabeth Warren, one of crypto’s sharpest critics, is expected to chair the Banking Committee when the new Congress is seated in January. The pairing of Democrats with Republicans could matter for confirmation. After the election, TD Cowen’s Jaret Seiberg told clients he did not expect Democrats to confirm Trump nominees

item.title: Most affairs don't matter except to the people involved. Ex-Nvidia CEO Jensen's blunder will rock the world
item.description: It's a story as old as time. Billionaire nerd boy meets girl. Girl is later suspected of being a spy. News at 11. Oh, and it's also been reported that he was having an affair with one of his direct-report employees. When Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang makes a "romantic" blunder, he doesn't do it halfway. The boss of the world's most valuable company – well, it was until recently, anyway – publicly resigned yesterday, November 12, as CEO, president, and board member, effective immediately. We don't know if he jumped or if he was pushed. He left after admitting to having an affair. Although he never named an affair partner, one of the affairs was reported to be with Alice Huang, AKA Huang Le. She's head of the Chinese company Megaspeed, which was an Nvidia partner. Megaspeed is accused of being a front for China's government that was used to transfer Nvidia chips to China, although this hasn't been proven. Some US officials also suspect [PDF] she's working for Chinese intelligence, although the DoJ said it hasn't yet reached a conclusion about this. The final nail in Jensen's coffin came when The New York Times reported he had also allegedly had an affair with Nvidia's VP of health care, Kimberly Powell. Jeeze, guy! In the aftermath, Nvidia's CFO, Colette Kress, was appointed interim CEO. She won't, I suspect, be in the job for long. CFOs are not CEOs. The jobs aren't remotely the same. In most companies, Huang would be replaced by the COO. That can't happen here. Nvidia doesn't have a COO. Both inside and outside of Nvidia, Huang is seen as Nvidia, and Nvidia as Huang. These days, billionaire CEOs are perceived as God-kings who know all and rule all. Much more often than not, that's BS. That isn't the case with Nvidia. Huang co-founded Nvidia on April 5, 1993. He was appointed CEO on day one, and he never left the job. At first, the company staggered forward. When it released the GeForce 256 in 1999 , which it marketed as the first GPU, it started on its path to becoming the chip manufacturer of choice for PC gamers. It still is today. That's a great niche, but it doesn't make a company a trillion-dollar business. No, the path to that dizzying height came when, in 2006, Nvidia unveiled CUDA . This programming architecture opened its GPUs' parallel-processing capabilities to scientific and other non-graphics workloads. From there, CUDA would become the foundation for most high-performance and AI computing. Huang was at the center of it all. He still was until now. At KubeCon North America , the trade show for Kubernetes, used in well over half of all AI projects, I spoke to many Nvidia employees. There were two things they all mentioned. First, they were in a state of shock. Maybe the top brass and government officials both in China and the US knew Huang was fooling with fire; the developer rank-and-file folks I spoke to hadn't had a clue. item.title: Muniz answers Murphy in three minutes as Fulham hold Newcastle
item.description: Newcastle spent most of Saturday afternoon looking for an opening at Craven Cottage. When Jacob Murphy finally curled the ball past Bernd Leno in the 80th minute, the visitors had a lead that lasted only 179 seconds. Rodrigo Muniz equalised for Fulham in the 83rd, leaving the sides with a 1-1 draw on 7 November 2026. Iwobi and Calvin Bassey both started for Fulham. The match went into the break goalless, a result that has to be kept separate from the full-time draw at betting sites in Cameroon , since the two selections cover different periods. The chances that went begging Fulham were lively early on. Oscar Bobb forced Lukáš Horníček into a save, and Gonzalo García glanced the following corner over. Newcastle soon found a route of their own. Harvey Barnes met an attack from Yoane Wissa and Will Osula, but Leno stopped his close-range finish with a foot. Barnes escaped again and tried to place the ball beyond the goalkeeper. This time Leno got his head to it. Newcastle thought they had scored from the resulting corner when Dan Burn turned in Murphy’s delivery. The goal was ruled out for a foul by Wissa on Timothy Castagne. The official score remained 0-0. It was hardly a first half without attacking chances. Fulham’s Alex Iwobi supplied a cross for Josh King, whose volley brought a sharp save from Horníček. Iwobi picked out King again near the interval, only for the header to go wide. Calvin Bassey also started for the home side, giving the match a second Nigerian international in Fulham’s lineup. The missed opportunities explain why Murphy’s eventual strike looked so decisive. Both goalkeepers had already made stops that could have changed the score considerably earlier. One careless pass, then the reply Newcastle’s goal began with Fulham losing possession in midfield. Murphy collected the loose pass, drove in from the right and bent a left-footed finish beyond Leno. After all the earlier saves, it took one mistake in possession to break the stalemate. Fulham did not leave much time for the away end to celebrate. A high regain put the ball into Shea Charles’s path; he moved it to substitute César Palacios. The attempted cross was blocked, but Muniz reacted to the loose ball and flicked it through a crowd near goal. Muniz had come off the bench earlier in the half. The Premier League said this was his first league goal in 28 matches. His finish came before Newcastle could settle into defending the advantage. Three scorelines, one match The last ten minutes made the score change twice, even though neither side took all three points. A selection covering Cameroon football also depends on the named period, not on which side led for part of the match. item.title: Kane takes Ballon d’Or as England’s wait finally ends
item.description: Twenty-five years after Michael Owen won it, the men’s Ballon d’Or belongs to an Englishman again. Harry Kane picked up the 2026 award at the London Palladium on 26 October, with 73 goals behind his claim. Real Madrid’s Kylian Mbappé finished second. Kane also left the ceremony with the Gerd Müller Trophy for the leading men’s goalscorer. Comparing a Ballon d’Or forecast through 1xbet South Sudan with a top-scorer selection involves two different results: one comes from a jury, the other from a goal count. Kane collected both honours in London, but they remain separate contests. The numbers behind the London announcement The goals came in two shirts. England Football’s account of the season separates his Bayern appearances from his international ones: Team Appearances Goals Bayern Munich, all competitions 51 61 England, all matches 14 12 Combined 65 73 The league supplied 36 goals in 31 appearances. Kane finished top of the Bundesliga scorers again, for the third year running. He added ten in the DFB-Pokal and one in the Supercup; his European haul was 14 as Bayern went as far as the Champions League semi-finals. Competition names also matter to sports betting in South Sudan , since Kane’s 61 club goals and 36 Bundesliga goals answer different questions. The Champions League figure is part of his club total, rather than an extra contribution to add on top. For England, six goals came in seven World Cup finals appearances. The national side finished third, its best placing since the 1966 victory. The remaining international goals in his season record came in qualifying and friendlies. Five came in five World Cup qualifiers, with another in two international friendly appearances, giving him 12 goals in 14 England outings overall. Bayern’s three domestic trophies give the goals some context, too. They kept the league title and lifted the DFB-Pokal, after winning the Franz Beckenbauer Supercup. The Ballon d’Or case included a team collecting silverware while Kane supplied the finishing. Owen’s wait ends, and Bayern’s too Kane becomes the fifth English player to receive the Ballon d’Or. The four names before him cover very different chapters of the award: 1956: Stanley Matthews took the first award. 1966: Bobby Charlton added it to his World Cup year. 1978 and 1979: Kevin Keegan won twice with Hamburg. 2001: Michael Owen brought it to Liverpool. Owen’s victory had remained the last English success for a quarter of a century. Kane’s award adds another name to that short list rather than another win for a previous recipient. Bayern had been waiting even longer. Karl-Heinz Rummenigge was their last winner, back in 1981. The Munich line now runs from Gerd Müller and Franz Beckenbauer through Rummenigge to Kane. There was recognition for another current Bayern player near the top of the voting, with Michael Olise finishing ninth. Kane’s own award nevertheless ends a 45-year gap for the club, stretching well beyond the careers of its present squad. A vote t

item.title: Yiaga Africa: Youth participation in 2027 elections declines by 20%
item.description: Yiaga Africa, an NGO, says the number of young people under 35 expected to participate in the forthcoming general elections has declined by a further 20 per cent, in spite of the enactment of the Not Too Young to Run law. The Executive Director, Yiaga Africa, Dr Samson Itodo, made this known at the Ready To Run Bootcamp for young candidates of political parties under the age of 35 years in Lagos on Friday. The News Agency of Nigeria reports that the programme, which is funded by the European Union, has the theme: “Ready to Run Bootcamp: From Aspiration to Representation”. Itodo, represented by its Programme Coordinator, Mr Ibrahim Faruk, said that following the passage of the law in 2019 by President Muhammadu Buhari, young people under 35 constituted 38 per cent of candidates in the 2019 general elections The executive director said that the percentage further dropped to about 28 per cent in 2023. Itodo attributed the decline to the high costs for nomination forms, campaigning, along with party structures and primary control among others. The executive director added that this leaned toward established interests, which had pushed young people to the margins and made securing political tickets difficult. He said: “The first thing Yiaga is doing is what we are doing here today, you know, there is the narrative that says young people are not ready to run. “Yiaga Africa is also changing that narrative to say young people are ready to run, and we are doing that through the Ready to Run boot camps to ensure that young people are ready to run. “​We have also done a lot of electoral reform advocacy; a lot of the changes to the Electoral Act have been as a result of advocacy. ​”While there have been attempts to reduce the high cost of nominations, also ensure that parties are more democratic and inclusive in a way that supports young people. “​Some of these advocacy efforts have been fruitful, some of them have taught us lessons. “We will continue to advocate for an electoral process that accommodates more young people, is more inclusive, less expensive and as democratic as possible,” he said. ​Itodo urged INEC and stakeholders to emphasise on ensuring a credible, secure, and logistically sound electoral process that the outcomes would reflect the will of the people. He also urged young Nigerians to collect their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs), participate fully and peacefully as voters, candidates, or agents, and refuse to sit out the democratic process. In his remarks, the Founder, African Governance Institute for Development, Mr Seyi Adisa admitted that running for office was more difficult for young people, as elections required not only financial resources but also “social capital”. According to him, while older individuals generally have more experience and social capital, young people can win elections. “It is more difficult, but achievable with the right strategies, networks, coalitions, and alliances,”he said. item.title: Scientists warn 1.5°C climate change threshold could arrive by 2029
item.description: ANTALYA, Turkey—Amid upbeat green-tech pep talks and notices for happy hours at the annual United Nations COP31 climate change conference on Thursday, two new reports offered a stark reminder of how far the world remains from containing global warming. Climate Action Tracker , a nonprofit group that analyzes climate policies, found that the planet is still on track to warm nearly 5 degrees Fahrenheit by 2100, a rise that would devastate coral reefs, disrupt agriculture and forests and melt most of the world’s ice. In a separate bulletin, the European Union’s Copernicus climate change service reported that global warming has accelerated significantly since the 2015 Paris climate agreement . When the Paris agreement was adopted, the average global temperature was projected to surpass the pact’s long-term threshold of 2.7 degrees Fahrenheit above the preindustrial average around 2045. After another decade of global climate summits, warming is now projected to cross that benchmark as soon as 2029, according to Copernicus. Read full article Comments

item.title: Ebola: Nigeria records zero secondary infections as 62 contacts exit monitoring
item.description: … Index patient recovers, discharged in Switzerland By Chioma Obinna Nigeria has recorded zero secondary transmission of the deadly Bundibugyo Virus Disease, a form of Ebola, following the successful completion of the 21-day monitoring period for all 62 contacts linked to the imported case confirmed in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) on October 20, 2026. The Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) yesterday announced that the last contact had been discharged from monitoring, with none of the 62 individuals developing the disease. In another development, the index patient, who was medically evacuated to Switzerland on October 26 for further treatment, has recovered, subsequently tested negative for the virus and been discharged from hospital. However, the NCDC warned that the successful completion of contact monitoring does not amount to a formal declaration that the outbreak is over, insisting that Nigeria must sustain heightened surveillance amid continued Ebola transmission in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC). Director-General of NCDC, Dr Jide Idris, who announced the development, described the outcome as encouraging, crediting early detection, prompt investigation and cooperation between health authorities and affected communities. “The 21-day monitoring period for contacts linked to the index case has been completed, with the last contact discharged today. We are glad to announce that none of the contacts became ill with the disease, meaning no transmission from the index case,” Idris said. He disclosed that 13 of the 62 contacts reported fever or other non-specific symptoms during the monitoring period. All 13 were tested for Bundibugyo Virus Disease and returned negative results. Similarly, seven alerts reported in Adamawa, Rivers, Borno, Lagos and Ekiti states within the last three weeks were investigated, with laboratory tests confirming that none was positive for the virus. The NCDC boss explained that the imported case was detected following an alert raised by healthcare workers through the agency’s event-based surveillance system, enabling the government to activate an emergency response and commence investigations. Under the leadership of the Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Professor Muhammad Ali Pate, the National Emergency Operations Centre was activated, while an Incident Management System was established to coordinate the response. According to Idris, the response focused on providing clinical care, identifying and monitoring exposed persons, preventing further transmission, protecting healthcare workers and strengthening disease surveillance. He said contact tracing covered healthcare facilities, households and other relevant settings, while infection prevention and control measures were reinforced in health facilities within the FCT and across the country. The agency also supported healthcare worker training and supplied personal protective equipment and other response materials to

item.title: 2027: Obanikoro confident of Tinubu, Hamzat’s victory
item.description: Sen. Musiliu Obanikoro, a chieftain of the All Progressives Congress (APC), has expressed confidence that President Bola Tinubu and the party’s governorship candidate in Lagos State, Dr Obafemi Hamzat, will emerge victorious in the 2027 general elections. Obanikoro, Director-General, PBAT-KOH Campaign Council, Lagos State, gave the expressed this while speaking during the Lagos SWAGA 2.0 Summit and launch in Lagos, on Friday. He said the party was well positioned to win Lagos, adding that the achievements of the Tinubu administration at the federal level and those of the Lagos State Government had endeared the APC to the electorate. “We are confident of victory. President Tinubu has shown leadership, and Hamzat has the experience and capacity to sustain the progress of Lagos. “Lagos residents know what good governance looks like, and they will not gamble with their future “I commend the grassroots mobilisation and initiative of SWAGA 2.0 for mobilising supporters to this event venue. “With this great turnout, massive victory is assured for Tinubu and APC gubernatorial candidate, Dr Obafemi Hamzat, ” he said. Obanikoro tasked party members to intensify grassroots mobilisation and ensure the party delivered 3.5 million votes for Tinubu and Hamzat in the state He said the target was achievable if members remained united, disciplined and committed to the party’s campaign structure. “Our target is 3.5 million votes. It is not just a number, it is a statement that Lagos stands firmly behind Tinubu and Hamzat,” he said. He urged party leaders at ward and local government levels to take the campaign to every polling unit and engage voters on the party’s achievements. Obanikoro said the opposition lacked the structure and credibility to challenge the APC in Lagos, describing the party as the only party with a clear vision for the state and the country. He called on supporters to shun violence and conduct issue-based campaigns, stressing that the APC would win through performance, not intimidation. “We must campaign with our records. We must not engage in violence. Our victory will come from the people because they have seen what we have done,” he said. He assured supporters that the party leadership would provide the necessary support to ensure a hitch-free campaign and victory at the polls. item.title: 95,000 PVCs uncollected in Plateau – INEC
item.description: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), says more 95,000 Permanent Voters Cards (PVCs) have not been collected in Plateau. Prof. Samuel Egwu, the Resident Electoral Commissioner (REC) in the state, disclosed this during a press conference on Friday in Jos. The REC explained that the uncollected PVCs were largely for those who registered before the 2023 general elections. Egwu, who said that the commission was worried over the large number of unclaimed PVCs in the state, urged voters to take advantage of the ongoing distribution exercise to collect their PVCs. “More than 95,000 PVCs from 2023 were still with our Electoral Officers across the state. “We call on who those who registered before the last general elections to come and collect their PVCs to enable them participate in the 2027 general elections,”he advised. The REC said that PVCs from the first phase of the Continuous Voter Registration (CVR) exercise conducted between August and December 2025, were made available for collection at INEC offices across the 17 Local Government Areas (LGAs) of the state. He said particularly that the PVCs of Shendam, Langtang North, Jos South and Kanam, were now available for collection. “More than 19,000 PVCs for those who applied for transfers and corrections are also available for collection. “All PVCs for the second phase of CVR conducted between January and April, are available and have been taken to the 17 LGAs for collection. “PVCs for the third phase of CVR are not ready, but will be made available before the end of November for collection,”he said. Egwu also disclosed that all non-sensitive materials for the 2027 general elections were available at the INEC office in Jos and would soon be distributed to the 17 LGAs. He further said that training of electoral officers who were not trained in 2023 had commenced. The REC reiterated INEC’s readiness to conduct a credible election in 2027. The post 95,000 PVCs uncollected in Plateau – INEC appeared first on Vanguard News .

Banire,a former commissioner of transportation in Lagos,made the call during the SWAGA 2.0 Summit and official launch in Ikeja, on Friday. He said political rallies alone were not sufficient to secure electoral victory. The chieftain said there was need for sustained grassroots mobilisation and direct engagement with voters. According to him, campaigns should not be characterised by abuses, confrontation or unnecessary political arguments but should focus on educating the electorate about government policies, programmes and achievements. “Rallies are not what win elections. What wins elections is going from door to door, engaging the people and explaining to them what the government has achieved. “Campaigns should not be about abusing opponents or engaging in fights. They should be about educating the electorate and convincing voters with facts about the performance of the present administration,” he said. Banire urged SWAGA leadership to establish functional campaign teams across all wards, local government areas and local council development areas in the South-West to strengthen grassroots mobilisation. He advised the organisation to compile and coordinate information on registered All Progressives Congress (APC) voters in the various communities to facilitate effective voter engagement and mobilisation. “SWAGA must ensure that it has representatives in every ward and local government area. You must know your people, understand the voting strength in each locality and develop a strategy for reaching them. “Wherever members or campaign agents encounter challenges in the course of their assignments, they should report such issues to their respective leaders for prompt attention and necessary solutions,” he said. The former commissioner emphasised the importance of appointing competent and literate campaign agents who could communicate effectively with residents and provide accurate information about government policies and achievements. He added that campaign and party agents must be able to read, write and understand the issues they are expected to communicate to the electorate. Banire expressed confidence that the South-West would deliver at least 70 per cent of its votes to President Tinubu in the 2027 presidential election if party members remained committed to effective grassroots mobilisation. Banire mentioned some of the infrastructure projects and economic reforms undertaken by the Tinubu administration, including the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway and the Badagry-Sokoto Coastal Road, describing them as significant interventions capable of promoting economic growth and national development. item.description: The National Youth Council of Nigeria (NYCN), Lagos State Chapter, has warned youths against allowing themselves to be recruited or manipulated into political thuggery. The youth organisation gave the warning following the attack on supporters of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) during a town hall meeting in Lagos. The council’s Chairman,Ibrahim Adigun, spoke with the interview with the News Agency of Nigeria on Friday in Lagos. Adigun said no amount of financial inducement or promise of political patronage was worth the life, freedom or future of any young person. He urged Lagos youths to recognise their importance as stakeholders in the democratic process and channel their energies towards peaceful political participation, civic responsibility and nation-building. “No amount of financial inducement or promise of political patronage is worth a life, a criminal record or a future destroyed. “As young people, we must recognise that we are stakeholders in the democratic process and we should channel our energy towards peaceful participation, civic responsibility and nation-building. “For emphasis, the NYCN Lagos State Chapter maintains its unequivocal opposition to political thuggery, electoral violence and every form of intimidation,” he said. Adigun said the council would continue to advocate peaceful political participation, responsible youth engagement and an electoral environment where every citizen could freely express their political choices without fear. He described the attack on NDC supporters as a serious threat to democratic participation, peaceful political engagement and the safety of citizens. According to him, political differences, no matter how deeply held, must never be settled through violence, intimidation or destruction of property. He expressed sympathy with those injured or otherwise affected by the incident, particularly young people, and wished them a speedy and full recovery. The NYCN chairman urged the relevant authorities to identify and bring those responsible for the attack to justice. He also appealed to political parties, candidates and their supporters to embrace civility and tolerance as political activities ahead of the 2027 general elections gathered momentum. “Campaigns should be driven by ideas, policies, track records and credible alternatives capable of addressing the concerns of Nigerians, particularly young people,” he said. Adigun called on security agencies, particularly the Lagos State Police Command, to strengthen security arrangements around political gatherings and other public events. He urged the agencies to remain professional, impartial and proactive in identifying potential threats, preventing attacks and protecting lives and property, irrespective of political affiliations. The chairman also reiterated the council’s commitment to opposing political thuggery, electoral violence and all forms of intimidation. item.title: Bitcoin Price Briefly Crashes to $67,500, Lowest Since August, as Dollar Holds 19-Month High
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Price Briefly Crashes to $67,500, Lowest Since August, as Dollar Holds 19-Month High Bitcoin price traded near $69,800 on Friday morning after briefly crashing to about $67,555 around midnight Eastern, its lowest level since mid-August, according to Bitcoin Magazine Pro data. The rebound held after October producer prices rose less than economists had expected, though the U.S. dollar remained near a 19-month high and traders still fully priced a December Federal Reserve rate hike. Bitcoin price was trading near $72,800 at this time Thursday. It slipped toward $71,000 by Thursday evening, then gave way late at night, breaking below $70,000 and sliding to that midnight low. The move also pushed the bitcoin price below its 200-week moving average , a long-term trend line near $68,000. Buyers lifted it back above $69,000 before sunrise, and the rebound extended toward $69,800 after the producer-price report. A stronger dollar and higher yields weigh on the bitcoin price The U.S. Dollar Index held above 103 Friday after a three-day rally took it to its highest level since April 2025. The 10-year Treasury yield was near 5.15% ahead of the data, and two-year yields, which track Fed expectations most closely, were on pace for their worst week since 2024, Bloomberg reported. Traders still see an 88% chance of a quarter-point hike at the Fed’s Dec. 8-9 meeting and a 12% chance of a half-point move, CME FedWatch data show . Fed Governor Christopher Waller has added a 50-basis-point increase to the discussion, and New York Fed President John Williams said Thursday that inflation remains high and policymakers need to take further action. Higher rates raise the cost of holding an asset that pays no interest, and a stronger dollar tends to drain demand for risk assets. Both have pressured the bitcoin price since this week’s hotter-than-expected consumer price index. Bitcoin has also broken from tech stocks. It fell 5.9% between Nov. 5 and Nov. 12 while the Nasdaq 100 gained 6.4%, a sign it is trading more on yields and the dollar than on the AI trade. Nasdaq 100 futures were up about 0.6% Friday after the producer-price report, as investors also weighed Nvidia’s announcement that Jensen Huang had resigned as CEO. Leverage unwinds and ETF selling continues The break below $70,000 set off a wave of forced selling. About $1.64 billion in crypto positions were liquidated over 24 hours, with bets on higher prices making up nearly 89% of the total and bitcoin positions accounting for $916 million. U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs added to the pressure. The funds posted about $47.7 million in net outflows Thursday, their sixth straight day of withdrawals, bringing the run to roughly $1.49 billion. BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) alone bled about $2 billion over nine sessions through Wednesday, and the group has now flipped to about $1.56 billion in net outflows for 2026. Sentiment has soured with it. A widely watched crypto fear and greed gauge

item.title: Oh my Word! Microsoft retires compatibility options, because who needs layouts to stay put
item.description: Microsoft is retiring some legacy layout settings in Word, potentially rearranging documents created or last saved in Word 2010 or earlier. "Affected documents may show layout differences, such as text reflow, changes in spacing or page count, or images and shapes moving to another page," the Windows biz said . The advice, if silly little things like page layout in a document matter, is to "consider exporting it to PDF before the change." Compatibility Mode lets a newer version of Word open a document created in an older version, such as Word 2010, without changing its layout. Newer features are switched off while the document is open this way. Users can convert the document to unlock newer features, although people using older versions of Word may then have difficulty editing parts of it. Microsoft has not identified the individual settings being retired, saying only: "We are retiring a set of compatibility options in Microsoft Word (desktop app) for documents in Compatibility Mode." The reason? "To simplify how Word handles document layout and provide a more consistent experience across platforms." Administrators may therefore want to check older templates, forms, and other documents whose pagination needs to stay put. The change is due to begin rolling out in the Windows version of Word from December 2026 and be completed by January 2027. The Mac version will follow in early 2027. Microsoft Word is more than 40 years old, and its first Windows version was released as the 1980s drew to a close. The word processor has evolved over the decades and is a mainstay of Microsoft's productivity suite. Compatibility Mode helps keep older documents from having their layouts abruptly borked the way Word does so well . Losing some of those safeguards could give administrators a fresh batch of "what the heck has happened to this document?" tickets as the change rolls out. ®

item.title: Quantum Systems drones back in the air after malware scare
item.description: Quantum Systems says its drones are flying again with Germany's military after a cyberattack prompted a precautionary grounding. The company says it spotted the attack at the end of October and reported it to the relevant authorities, but disclosed few details about the intrusion. "The threat was contained thanks to the swift response of our IT and security teams in close and transparent collaboration with the authorities," it said on Thursday. "Through the quick measures taken and the characteristics of the incident, there is no risk in operating Quantum Systems' unmanned systems for the end users and the operators." It added that other players in the European defense industry, and those who support Ukraine's military efforts, have faced "persistent cyberattacks for years." The Bundeswehr grounded its Quantum Systems drones after malware was detected in an update to QBase, the company's QBase ground-control software, Der Spiegel reported, citing unnamed sources. QBase lets operators plan missions, monitor flights, and process data from the ground. The malicious update reportedly reached servers belonging to the German military and other customers, but did not directly infect the drones. "The fleet is operating normally around the globe – including Germany and the Bundeswehr," Quantum Systems told Reuters . "The Bundeswehr was the only customer to ground their systems as a precaution." A spokesperson for Germany's defense ministry declined to comment on the attack or the reported details. The Register asked Quantum Systems for further details. Founded in 2015, Quantum Systems has been providing drones to the Ukrainian war effort for years. Last month, Chancellor Friedrich Merz announced funding for "several tens of thousands" of the company's interceptor drones as part of Germany's winter aid package. The new drones will be built in Ukraine and support interceptor systems already in use on the front lines. Quantum Systems announced a $1.2 billion Series D funding round in July, valuing the company at around $8 billion. ®

item.title: FWIFT 2026 Convention Communique: Industry Leaders Charge Women in Media to Embrace Cross-Border Growth
item.description: The Forum for Women in Film and Television Nigeria (FWIFT) successfully concluded its 2026 annual convention on Thursday, October 29, at the historic Glover Memorial Hall in Lagos, Nigeria. Convening under the theme “One Industry, Many Voices: Building Together,” the afternoon brought together over 200 practitioners from several sectors including; film, television, radio, advertising, and digital media to connect, share insights, and build mutual agency. Supported by the African Women’s Development Fund (AWDF) , the convention featured a keynote address by cultural curator Sandra Mbanefo Obiago , interactive panel sessions, break-out workshops, speed networking, and a flagship fireside chat titled “The Cross Over: A Career Beyond Borders.” The event drew leading voices from across the creative economy, including media executive Kadaria Ahmed , filmmaker Biodun Stephens, media personality Gbemi Olateru-Olagbegi, executive director Rosemary Egabor-Afolahan, and director Esosa Osagiede. Key takeaways and actionable resolutions from the convention sessions emphasized resilience, strategic partnerships, and structural evolution: Embrace Bold Collaboration and Risk-Taking: Speakers urged media professionals to shed apprehension around institutional partnerships. As highlighted during the panel discussions: “Do not allow fear of failing stop you from asking for help, do your due diligence on the people you want to partner with then go for it. If it does not work, do not stop, get up and go again.” Adaptability as a Survival Imperative: In an era of rapid technological and digital shifts across broadcast and film, participants were reminded of the absolute necessity of evolution: “If you don’t change with the times, you will grow stale.” Deconstructing Industry Myths: Addressing professional dynamics, panelists challenged antiquated narratives regarding female competition, affirming that systemic progress relies on solidarity: “Women work well with women, it is a myth that they do not.” FWIFT’s leadership noted that the conversations at Glover Memorial Hall mark a critical step toward cementing cross-sector alliances. The forum remains committed to translating these insights into actionable frameworks, mentorship programs, and policy advocacy for women shaping the future of African media. For more information on upcoming FWIFT initiatives, programs, and future events, visit the official website or follow @fwiftnigeria on social media. About FWIFT Nigeria The Forum For Women in Film and Television Nigeria (FWIFT) is a professional organization dedicated to empowering Nigerian women in screen-based, audio, and digital media through advocacy, skill acquisition, mentorship, and strategic networking. item.title: Double-catch drama: Why Starship's Flight 15 is so important to SpaceX
item.description: null Having reached orbit for the first time with Starship last time out, SpaceX is looking to take a huge stride toward full reusability with Flight 15 — the first attempt to catch the megarocket's Ship upper stage, as the company eyes hourly launches by 2030. SpaceX is targeting today (Nov. 13) for Starship 's 15th flight, which will lift off from the company's Starbas site in South Texas. If all goes well, the mission — which you can watch here at Space.com — will end on Saturday (Nov. 14) with the first attempt at what SpaceX itself calls the "Holy Grail of rocketry": Catching both Starship's Super Heavy booster and Ship upper stage chopstick-style back at the launch pad. "If successful, this will mark the first full recovery of an orbital launch system and a breakthrough moment in making Starship a reliable, rapidly reusable rocket," SpaceX wrote in its Flight 15 mission description . The 75-minute Flight 15 launch window opens today at 5:45 p.m. EST (2245 GMT), and a number of Starship firsts are planned for early in the flight. For example, while SpaceX has caught three Super Heavy boosters and reused two of them to date, the first attempt to catch a next-gen Super Heavy "V3" vehicle will come today, around 6.5 minutes after liftoff. If the Ship upper stage gets the go-ahead for orbital insertion, it will deploy 26 Starlink V3 satellites — designed especially for use on Starship — into low Earth orbit (LEO), starting about 35 minutes after launch. Then, 21 hours later, if "internally developed, and FAA-approved, conditions" for a return to Starbase and catch are met — including on-orbit assessment of Ship's heat shield by three of the V3 satellites — SpaceX will attempt to recover the orbital upper stage. This landmark try will follow the first-ever Ship reentry over inhabited areas, as the vehicle will maneuver its way over sparsely populated regions of northern Mexico and southern Texas. (On previous missions, Ship has splashed down in the open ocean.) It will head back to Starbase and make a bellyflop maneuver as it descends to the site's Pad 2 before flipping itself vertical, ready for embrace of the launch tower's waiting mechanical arms. "SpaceX will attempt to catch both the Super Heavy booster and Starship on the upcoming flight. If both are successful, it will mark the first time that all parts of an orbital rocket return to Earth intact," Elon Musk said via X, the social media platform he owns, on Nov. 6 . "This is the critical breakthrough needed to make life multiplanetary." Composite photo showing the Super Heavy booster of SpaceX's Starship megarocket coming in for a landing on the launch mount on Oct. 13, 2024. (Image credit: SpaceX via X) The catch Half of the system is already proven. With catching and reflying boosters largely established, the next and unprecedented step is catching Ship. item.title: The scourge of femicide in Mexico: Impunity reigns in state of Morelos
item.description: When Claudia Sheinbaum became Mexico's first female president in 2024, she pledged to tackle violence against women. And while femicides have fallen since she took office, the numbers remain alarming, with around 520 murders so far this year. In the small state of Morelos, just outside the capital Mexico City, four female students have been murdered since January, including a Spanish woman on an exchange programme. The state has one of the highest femicide rates in the country.

item.title: Palantir adds three UK police forces to its beat with £10.1M deal
item.description: Three UK police forces led by Cambridgeshire Constabulary have awarded Palantir a £10.1 million contract after London Mayor Sadiq Khan blocked a separate deal with the Metropolitan Police. The five-year agreement covers Bedfordshire Police, Cambridgeshire Constabulary, and Hertfordshire Constabulary, despite warnings from campaigners and politicians about dependence on the supplier. A contract award notice says the east of England police forces expect the Palantir platform to provide "an enterprise-wide data integration and analytics capability, enabling the secure ingestion, linking, and analysis of data from multiple systems and sources across the policing environment." The contract runs until October 2031, with the estimated value covering all three forces. News of the award coincided with revelations that former Metropolitan Police commissioner Dame Cressida Dick has worked as a paid adviser to Palantir since September 2025. A Palantir spokesperson told the Bureau of Investigative Journalism : "Dame Cressida is advising us on how our software could help improve the delivery of services in the public sector, drawing on more than 40 years of public service in a variety of roles." Dick said her role was limited to advising on how such products could assist public services. She said she had never lobbied or advocated for Palantir, or introduced the company to her contacts. Dick led the Metropolitan Police, the UK's largest force, between 2017 and 2022. She left after Khan said he had lost confidence in her. She later said she was " intimidated " into leaving. Separately, Khan stepped in to block the Met from awarding a £50 million contract to Palantir. His office cited serious concerns about the procurement process. Palantir later sued the Met, but the case was settled in October. The new police contract award follows a report from MPs warning of vendor lock-in to US suppliers, including Palantir. It said : "Our view that Palantir's increasing presence across the public sector represents an unacceptable point of weakness is not ideologically motivated or driven by concerns about the quality of their products. "The government should retain the ability to pick and choose individual suppliers and safeguard against the risk of vendor lock-in and debilitating dependencies, particularly in areas of critical national importance such as healthcare and national security infrastructure." ®

item.title: Digital Credit: Comparing The Six Bitcoin Preferred Stocks
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Digital Credit: Comparing The Six Bitcoin Preferred Stocks Digital credit is an emerging asset class that transforms corporate Bitcoin balance sheets into income producing securities. Strategy pioneered the market with five perpetual preferred equity instruments: STRK, STRF, STRD, STRC, and STRE (the first four are listed in the U.S.). Strive subsequently introduced SATA and SATS, bringing the category to six U.S. instruments across two issuers. These securities offer investors preferred equity (read: credit-like) exposure to companies whose balance sheets are dominated by Bitcoin. Their perpetual structure means investors principally rely on recurring dividends and the continued financial strength of the issuer. Unlike term debt, there is no maturation date at which the full principal is ever paid back. Evaluating digital credit requires examining four characteristics: creditworthiness, investor protections, liquidity, and dividend profile. This article explains all four dimensions and then offers a ranking for the six digital credit instruments along these lines. None of this should be taken as investment advice—it is only a systematic framework for analyzing digital credit. 1. Creditworthiness Creditworthiness measures an issuer’s ability to support its financial obligations. Traditional credit analysis focuses on earnings, free cash flow, and refinancing capacity. Companies with strong cash generation can service interest and repay maturing debt. Digital credit issuers today derive financial strength primarily from their Bitcoin reserves, placing greater emphasis on net asset coverage. In the future we could certainly see digital credit issuers that also have significant cash flows on top of Bitcoin holdings, which would add to creditworthiness. The central question is how much Bitcoin supports each dollar of credit obligations. One useful measure is the BTC Rating , which compares the dollar value of Bitcoin reserves with the outstanding credit, accounting for the seniority of each credit instrument. Cash reserves can further strengthen creditworthiness by reducing net obligations. For example, a 5x BTC Rating indicates five dollars of Bitcoin supporting every dollar of notional credit claims. Higher ratings provide greater protection against Bitcoin price declines. Seniority matters because instruments from the same issuer can have different claims on the same asset base. A senior preferred instrument benefits from greater coverage than a junior preferred instrument: all senior claims are included in the BTC Rating calculation of a junior instrument. Creditworthiness also depends on corporate governance and capital allocation. Management must preserve sufficient Bitcoin coverage while funding recurring dividends. Issuing additional credit increases dividend obligations, while assets accumulation (Bitcoin or cash) strengthen the asset base. item.title: Ayobami Esther Akinnagbe: Organisational Mistakes Start-up Founders Should Avoid
item.description: Two women engaged in a professional meeting, discussing business in a modern office setting. Image by RDNE Stock project for Pexels . There is a lot that goes into establishing a successful business. It requires developing the business idea, securing clients, building a customer base and eventually bringing people on board. Starting a business and watching it grow can be an exciting experience. However, one thing many start-up founders overlook is the importance of having the right organisational structure in place. It is one thing to have a great business idea and attract talented employees, but it is another thing to create an environment where everyone understands their responsibilities, knows who they report to and can work effectively towards achieving the company’s objectives. I once worked with a client who needed a new set of employees for a business establishment that was reopening after a period of restructuring. As part of the recruitment process, the first thing I ensured was that a manager was hired before proceeding to fill the remaining vacancies. The idea was simple. The manager would oversee the day-to-day running of the establishment, ensure that company policies were implemented and periodically train employees based on the requirements of their respective roles. During the recruitment process, I clearly communicated each employee’s responsibilities and the person they would be reporting to. These details were also stated in their respective offer letters, so everyone understood their roles and the management structure they were expected to work within. However, there was a challenge. Before the manager was hired, an accountant who was personally known to both co-founders had also been in charge of the previous employees. Following the restructuring, the founders had communicated their desire for a new operational arrangement, and this was clearly reflected in the recruitment brief. Although the new employees understood that they were expected to report to the newly hired manager, the existing employees still had their loyalty to the accountant, who had previously been in charge. The challenge was that the new management structure had not been properly implemented within the organisation. Consequently, the manager was expected to take charge of the establishment without the necessary authority and cooperation from everyone involved. This created unnecessary friction, and I found myself having to mediate whenever issues arose, even though the service I had been engaged to provide was recruitment. I eventually had a lengthy conversation with one of the founders, explaining that communicating reporting lines and responsibilities during recruitment was only one part of the process. The organisation also needed to formally implement the new structure, clarify authority and ensure that everyone understood and respected the changes.
